lessons.title: School types and the school day
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I describe my school and my school day clearly and accurately?
objectives: Name types of school
Tell the time and describe the timetable
Compare in-person and online schooling
successCriteria: All: say what kind of school you attend and when it starts and ends
Most: use ordinal numbers for times and number-noun agreement for lessons
Some: compare two kinds of school with reasons
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography and Citizenship: education around the world
lessons.smsc: Spiritual and social: the value of seeking knowledge ('ilm); gratitude for education
starter: Bismillah. Retrieval: say 'I want to study engineering at university' in Arabic.
Write the Arabic for 'two nights' and 'three nights'.
Give the comparative of كَبِيرٌ and say 'my town is bigger than your town'.

teach.heading: Types of school
teach.note: Start of Year 11 and Theme 3 (School). Pupils name their own school type first; for TGA pupils this includes an online school, so be inclusive and allow 'I study online'. The words are adjectives agreeing with مَدْرَسَةٌ (feminine). لِلْبَنِينَ is 'for boys' and لِلْبَنَاتِ 'for girls'. Drill choral then pupils personalise.

teach.heading: The school day
bullets: تَبْدَأُ الدُّرُوسُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ
Lessons start at nine o'clock
وَتَنْتَهِي فِي الثَّالِثَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ
and finish at half past three
عِنْدَنَا سِتُّ حِصَصٍ وَاسْتِرَاحَةٌ
We have six lessons and a break
teach.note: Teach times with the feminine ordinal (التَّاسِعَةُ, الثَّالِثَةُ) because السَّاعَةُ is feminine. 'At' = فِي (or عِنْدَ). 'Half past' = وَالنِّصْفِ. For lessons: سِتُّ حِصَصٍ (6 lessons) because حِصَّةٌ is feminine, so the number drops its ta marbuta. Plural subjects that are not people (الدُّرُوسُ) take a feminine SINGULAR verb: تَبْدَأُ. Recycle numbers and the dual.

teach.heading: In person or online?

left.title: A school building
points: I meet my friends every day

right.title: Online school
points: I study from home and save time

teach.note: This supports the 'advantages and disadvantages' question and respects pupils at an online school. Prompt: which statements would your friends make? Add a reason with لِأَنَّ. Practise connecting with وَلَكِنْ and بَيْنَمَا (whereas). Keep language tied to what pupils can say and write in the exam: 2 to 3 sentences per answer.

teach.heading: Model: describing my school

model.problem: Say: 'I study at a mixed state school. Lessons start at half past eight and finish at three. We have five lessons and a break.'
steps: 'I study at a mixed state school' = أَدْرُسُ فِي مَدْرَسَةٍ حُكُومِيَّةٍ مُخْتَلَطَةٍ
'Lessons start at half past eight' = تَبْدَأُ الدُّرُوسُ فِي الثَّامِنَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ
'and finish at three' = وَتَنْتَهِي فِي الثَّالِثَةِ
'five lessons and a break' = عِنْدَنَا خَمْسُ حِصَصٍ وَاسْتِرَاحَةٌ
model.answer: أَدْرُسُ فِي مَدْرَسَةٍ حُكُومِيَّةٍ مُخْتَلَطَةٍ. تَبْدَأُ الدُّرُوسُ فِي الثَّامِنَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ وَتَنْتَهِي فِي الثَّالِثَةِ. عِنْدَنَا خَمْسُ حِصَصٍ وَاسْتِرَاحَةٌ.

teach.note: Model aloud, then pupils say it back with their own details. Notice the three parts: type, timetable, opinion. The opinion gives an extra mark in a conversation. Remind them to vary the sentence openings.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'The lessons finish at three'?
check.why: تَنْتَهِي = finishes; the feminine ordinal الثَّالِثَةِ is used for the hour. A means 'start'; C uses the masculine ordinal; D has a plural human verb for a non-human subject.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A is 'start'; C has the masculine ordinal; D has a masculine verb with a non-human plural. Ask pupils to give the reason for each rejection.

practice: Say the type of your school and when it starts and finishes.
Write the Arabic: 'We have four lessons and a break.'
Say one advantage and one disadvantage of studying online.
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about your school and school day.
Extend: add a comparison with another kind of school.
Stretch: write 100 words describing your ideal school day and explain why.
exit: Write: 'Lessons start at nine.'
Write one reason you like your school.
lessons.homework: Write 80 words about your school and school day. Include a time, a number of lessons and one opinion.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the time frames on a card and a clock to complete. Stretch: add a passive description (يُدَرَّسُ ...) and a contrast with بَيْنَمَا.

lessons.title: Subjects: what I study and what I think
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I give reasoned opinions about my school subjects?
objectives: Name school subjects
Give opinions using أَجِدُ ... + accusative
Justify with reasons about teachers and usefulness
successCriteria: All: say your favourite subject and one reason
Most: use أَجِدُ ... + noun and adjective with accusative endings
Some: write a balanced paragraph on three subjects
lessons.crossCurricular: All curriculum subjects; PSHE: study skills and aspirations
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: knowledge as a trust; humility in learning
starter: Retrieval: say the Arabic for 'the lessons start at nine'.
Write 'mixed school' and 'girls' school' in Arabic.
Say 'I like the film because it is enjoyable'.

teach.heading: School subjects
teach.note: Match the subject to pupils' timetable. Note the definite article is normally used with subject names in Arabic (الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ). Point out الْجُغْرَافِيَا (geography) and الْكِيمِيَاءُ as borrowed words. التَّرْبِيَةُ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةُ links to Islamic Studies. Practise in rapid fire: show a subject and pupils say it with 'I study ...' (أَدْرُسُ ...).

teach.heading: Opinion frames
bullets: مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ
My favourite subject is maths because it is enjoyable
أَجِدُ الْفِيزِيَاءَ صَعْبَةً وَلَكِنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ
I find physics difficult but it is useful
أَجِدُ التَّارِيخَ مُمْتِعًا لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ لَطِيفٌ
I find history interesting because the teacher is kind
teach.note: Teach the structure أَجِدُ + object + adjective: BOTH the object and the adjective are accusative (الْفِيزِيَاءَ صَعْبَةً; التَّارِيخَ مُمْتِعًا). That is the most rewarding structure here: it replaces repetitive 'I like'. In لِأَنَّ + sentence: after لِأَنَّ the subject is accusative (الْمُعَلِّمَ), but when the pronoun is attached the case disappears (لِأَنَّهَا). In لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ لَطِيفٌ the noun takes -a: say it aloud and ask pupils to spot the rule.

teach.heading: Model: three subjects, three opinions

model.problem: Say: 'My favourite subject is geography because it is useful. I find maths difficult, but I like the teacher.'
steps: 'My favourite subject is geography' = مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْجُغْرَافِيَا
'because it is useful' = لِأَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ
'I find maths difficult' = أَجِدُ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ صَعْبَةً
'but I like the teacher' = وَلَكِنَّنِي أُحِبُّ الْمُعَلِّمَ
model.answer: مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْجُغْرَافِيَا لِأَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ. أَجِدُ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ صَعْبَةً وَلَكِنَّنِي أُحِبُّ الْمُعَلِّمَ.

teach.note: Model the vocabulary of contrast (لَكِنَّ, بَيْنَمَا) and a final summary. Pupils tick the structures: favourite, find + adjective, reason. This sequence earns marks for opinion, justification and range. Ask pupils to rewrite with their own three subjects.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'I find history interesting'?
check.why: After أَجِدُ both the thing and its description are accusative: التَّارِيخَ مُمْتِعًا. A keeps nominative endings, B is 'he found', D is indefinite and nominative.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Distractors: nominative endings; a third-person past verb; a noun in the wrong case. Ask which endings give it away.

practice: Say three subjects you study and give one opinion about each.
Complete: أَجِدُ الْكِيمِيَاءَ ___ (difficult).
Translate: 'I like PE because the lessons are active (نَشِيطَةٌ).'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about your subjects with reasons.
Extend: add a comparison (أَسْهَلُ مِنْ) and a link word.
Stretch: write 100 words on which subject matters most for your future and why.
exit: Write: 'My favourite subject is history because it is interesting.'
Write: 'I find science useful.'
lessons.homework: Write a paragraph (80 words) on three subjects: one you love, one you find hard, one you find useful.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the subject table with images and the three frames. Stretch: add a conditional (لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ ... ) about adding another subject.

lessons.title: School rules, pressures and wellbeing
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I explain rules and pressure, and say what helps?
objectives: Express obligation, permission and prohibition
Describe pressures such as exams and homework
Suggest solutions using the present tense
successCriteria: All: say two rules in your school
Most: use يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ and يُمْنَعُ with the correct endings
Some: write about pressure and solutions in a balanced answer
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: mental health and wellbeing; Citizenship: rules and rights
lessons.smsc: Moral and spiritual: patience (ṣabr), reliance on Allah, balance and rest
starter: Retrieval: say your favourite subject and why.
Say 'I find geography useful'.
Write the Arabic for 'six lessons' and 'at half past three'.

teach.heading: Rules: must, may, may not

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَلْبَسَ الزِّيَّ الْمَدْرَسِيَّ
yajibu ʿalaynā an nalbasa z-ziyya l-madrasiyya
using the phone in class is forbidden
we are not allowed to leave

teach.note: Sort into three categories: obligation (يَجِبُ), permission (يُسْمَحُ), prohibition (يُمْنَعُ / لَا يُسْمَحُ). After يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ the verb is subjunctive: نَلْبَسَ, نَصِلَ. After يُمْنَعُ comes a verbal noun (اِسْتِخْدَامُ). Practise by giving real rules and asking 'must, may or banned?' Use pupils' real rules.

teach.heading: Pressures and solutions

left.title: Pressures
points: Exams cause a lot of pressure

right.title: What helps
points: I organise my time and rest

teach.note: Pupils identify which items are causes and which are solutions. Be sensitive: wellbeing may be a real issue for some pupils. Frame it as strategies, and remind pupils where to find help in school. The verb أَشْعُرُ بِـ (I feel) takes بِ + noun. Solutions use the present tense with أُنَظِّمُ and أَسْتَرِيحُ. Ask for a personal example without pressing disclosure.

teach.heading: Watch the verb after أَنْ

misconception.wrong: يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَصِلُ فِي الْوَقْتِ
misconception.right: يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَصِلَ فِي الْوَقْتِ - the verb after أَنْ takes -a

teach.note: Pupils recall the subjunctive from Year 10. Here it is applied to a plural verb 'we': نَصِلُ → أَنْ نَصِلَ. For verbs ending in -ūna the final nun drops (تَلْبَسُونَ → أَنْ تَلْبَسُوا). Practise with a set of rule sentences on the board.

teach.heading: Model: rules and pressure

model.problem: Say: 'In my school we must wear a uniform and phones are banned. Exams put a lot of pressure on me, so I organise my time.'
steps: 'we must wear a uniform' = يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَلْبَسَ الزِّيَّ الْمَدْرَسِيَّ
'phones are banned' = وَيُمْنَعُ اسْتِخْدَامُ الْهَاتِفِ
'Exams put a lot of pressure on me' = تُسَبِّبُ الِامْتِحَانَاتُ ضَغْطًا كَبِيرًا عَلَيَّ
'so I organise my time' = لِذَلِكَ أُنَظِّمُ وَقْتِي
model.answer: فِي مَدْرَسَتِي يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَلْبَسَ الزِّيَّ الْمَدْرَسِيَّ وَيُمْنَعُ اسْتِخْدَامُ الْهَاتِفِ. تُسَبِّبُ الِامْتِحَانَاتُ ضَغْطًا كَبِيرًا عَلَيَّ، لِذَلِكَ أُنَظِّمُ وَقْتِي.

teach.note: Read the model, then ask pupils to spot: an obligation, a prohibition, a cause and a solution. Then they change the details to match their own school. Stress that a solution after a problem is a mark-earning move in the conversation.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'We must arrive on time'?
options: يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَصِلُ فِي الْوَقْتِ
يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَصِلَ فِي الْوَقْتِ
check.why: يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ + subjunctive (نَصِلَ). A has the wrong ending, C misses أَنْ, D means it is forbidden.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A keeps the indicative; C omits أَنْ; D is a prohibition. Ask pupils to read each aloud.

practice: Say two rules in your school using يَجِبُ and يُمْنَعُ.
Give two causes of pressure and two solutions in Arabic.
Translate: 'I feel stressed because of the exams, so I talk to my teacher.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences on rules and pressures at your school.
Extend: add the reason for each rule.
Stretch: write 100 words giving your view on whether school rules are fair (عَادِلَةٌ) and why.
exit: Write: 'We are not allowed to eat in class.'
Write one thing that helps you when you feel stress.
lessons.homework: Write 80 words on school rules and pressure. Use يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ, يُمْنَعُ and a solution.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the three rule categories as a sorting task and the frames. Stretch: use the contrast بِالرَّغْمِ مِنْ أَنَّ ... (although ...).

lessons.title: Celebrating success and the passive voice
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I talk about achievements, and what does the passive add?
objectives: Describe achievements and awards
Recognise and form the past passive
Express gratitude for success in an Islamic way
successCriteria: All: say what you or others achieved
Most: use فَازَ بِ, نَجَحَ فِي and a past tense verb accurately
Some: use the past passive كُرِّمَ / مُنِحَ with correct agreement
lessons.crossCurricular: English: formal writing and the passive; Citizenship: recognising achievement
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: 'al-ḥamdu lillāh' and attributing success to Allah; humility
starter: Retrieval: say 'we must wear the uniform' in Arabic.
Say 'using the phone is forbidden'.
Give the past of سَافَرَ for 'I' and 'we'.

teach.heading: Success vocabulary
teach.note: Link to the end-of-year awards at their school or at TGA. فَازَ is hollow: فُزْتُ, فُزْنَا. نَجَحَ is followed by فِي: نَجَحْتُ فِي الِامْتِحَانِ. Elicit examples of 'ceremony' language: حَفْلٌ, تَكْرِيمٌ. Use 'al-ḥamdu lillāh' after success: it is part of adab. Pupils say one success in their own life.

teach.heading: The past passive
teach.note: Introduce the passive as a Higher-tier feature that pupils must RECOGNISE in reading and may use in writing. The vowel pattern is u-i: the first letter takes damma and the second kasra (كُتِبَ). The agent is not mentioned. The object becomes the subject (nominative) and the verb agrees with it: مُنِحَتْ سَارَةُ (feminine). Show on the board how the vowels change. The written exam does not require vowels, so pupils need context to see the passive.

teach.heading: Model: active to passive

model.problem: Say: 'At the end of the year the school honoured the top students and gave them certificates. I won a prize in maths, al-ḥamdu lillāh.'
steps: 'the school honoured the top students' = كَرَّمَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ الطُّلَّابَ الْمُتَفَوِّقِينَ
Passive version: كُرِّمَ الطُّلَّابُ الْمُتَفَوِّقُونَ
'and gave them certificates' = وَمَنَحَتْهُمْ شَهَادَاتٍ (passive: وَمُنِحُوا شَهَادَاتٍ)
'I won a prize in maths' = فُزْتُ بِجَائِزَةٍ فِي الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
model.answer: كَرَّمَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ الطُّلَّابَ الْمُتَفَوِّقِينَ وَمَنَحَتْهُمْ شَهَادَاتٍ. فُزْتُ بِجَائِزَةٍ فِي الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.

teach.note: Show the same event twice. The passive is common in news-style texts and school notices. Pupils translate both sentences and decide when the passive is better (when the doer is unknown or unimportant). Finish with gratitude.

teach.heading: Success comes from Allah

quote.text: وَمَا تَوْفِيقِي إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ'My success is only through Allah.'

teach.note: Use for reflection, not an Arabic grammar point. Surah Hud 11:88, the closing part of the statement of Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him). Teacher: check the wording against a mushaf before display. Discuss: how does this attitude balance effort and gratitude? Pupils may annotate the words 'tawfīqī' (my success) and 'billāh' (through Allah).

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'The student was honoured'?
check.why: The passive كُرِّمَ has damma then kasra, and the student is the subject (nominative). A means 'he honoured the student', C 'he honours the student', D 'I honoured the student'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. B is active with the object; C is present tense; D has the wrong person. Ask pupils which vowel pattern tells them it is passive.

practice: Give the passive of: فَتَحَ, كَتَبَ, كَرَّمَ.
Say: 'She passed the exam and won a prize' and 'The prize was given to Sara.'
Role play: congratulate a friend who won a prize (مَبْرُوكٌ!).
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about achievements at your school.
Extend: write two sentences in the passive.
Stretch: write a 100-word report on a prize-giving ceremony in the past tense.
exit: Write: 'I passed the exam, al-ḥamdu lillāh.'
Turn into the passive: كَرَّمَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ الطَّالِبَةَ.
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word news article for the school website about an award ceremony. Use the passive twice.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the active/passive table and the frame كُرِّمَ ___ لِأَنَّهُ ___. Stretch: use passive forms in the present (يُكَرَّمُ) and future.

lessons.title: School trips
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I describe a trip I went on and write about it in a letter?
objectives: Use trip vocabulary
Tell a past-tense story with new verb forms
Write an informal message and a formal letter opening and closing
successCriteria: All: say where the trip was and what you did
Most: use اِسْتَمْتَعْنَا and اِلْتَقَطْنَا and give an opinion
Some: write a formal letter of 90 words about a trip
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography and History: fieldwork and visits; English: letter writing
lessons.smsc: Social and cultural: learning through visits; respect for places visited
starter: Retrieval: say 'The student was honoured' in Arabic.
Say 'I passed the exam'.
Give the I and we past forms of ذَهَبَ.

teach.heading: Trip vocabulary and verbs

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: we went on a trip to a museum

teach.note: Pupils talk about a real trip they went on, with their school or online school if available. Introduce the new past-tense forms. Pattern note: اِسْتَمْتَعْنَا and اِلْتَقَطْنَا begin with alif wasla and are Forms X and VIII, so the endings are the same regular -nā / -tu. Pupils conjugate اِسْتَمْتَعَ and اِلْتَقَطَ for 'I'.

teach.heading: Informal and formal

right.title: Formal (to the headteacher)
points: حَضْرَةَ الْمُدِيرِ الْمُحْتَرَمَ، تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ
Dear respected Headteacher, greetings, and now to the matter

teach.note: Pupils choose the register. Informal = to a friend; formal = to a headteacher or a company. Show which phrases belong to which side. For the exam, writers are expected to match register to the audience. Pupils sort the phrases and then add one more of each.

teach.heading: Model: writing about the trip

model.problem: Write: 'Dear Sami, last week we went on a school trip to the museum. We took photos and the guide explained a lot. The trip was useful and I enjoyed it. Best wishes, Yusuf.'
steps: Greeting: عَزِيزِي سَامِي
'last week we went on a trip to the museum' = الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِيَ ذَهَبْنَا فِي رِحْلَةٍ مَدْرَسِيَّةٍ إِلَى الْمَتْحَفِ
'We took photos and the guide explained' = اِلْتَقَطْنَا صُوَرًا وَشَرَحَ لَنَا الْمُرْشِدُ الْكَثِيرَ
'The trip was useful and I enjoyed it' = كَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ مُفِيدَةً وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُ بِهَا
Closing: مَعَ أَطْيَبِ التَّحِيَّاتِ، يُوسُفُ
model.answer: عَزِيزِي سَامِي، الْأُسْبُوعَ الْمَاضِيَ ذَهَبْنَا فِي رِحْلَةٍ مَدْرَسِيَّةٍ إِلَى الْمَتْحَفِ. اِلْتَقَطْنَا صُوَرًا وَشَرَحَ لَنَا الْمُرْشِدُ الْكَثِيرَ. كَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ مُفِيدَةً وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُ بِهَا. مَعَ أَطْيَبِ التَّحِيَّاتِ، يُوسُفُ

teach.note: Model a short email to a friend. Notice: the greeting, the past narrative, a description with كَانَتْ, an opinion and a future link. Pupils highlight each part. Note الرِّحْلَةُ is feminine, so كَانَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ مُفِيدَةً.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which verb means 'we enjoyed'?
check.why: The ending -nā marks 'we'. اِسْتَمْتَعْتُ is 'I enjoyed', اِسْتَمْتَعُوا 'they enjoyed', يَسْتَمْتِعُ 'he enjoys'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Distractors are I, they and present. Ask pupils to underline the ending that shows 'we'.

practice: Say three things you did on a trip using nā verbs.
Write a greeting and closing for an informal email and a formal letter.
Translate: 'We took photos and learnt a lot.'
independent: Core: write a 6-sentence email to a friend about a trip.
Extend: add an opinion and a future plan (next year we will visit ...).
Stretch: write a 100-word formal letter to the headteacher suggesting a new trip.
exit: Write: 'The trip was very useful.'
Write one formal greeting in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Write an email (80 words) to a friend about a school trip. Use at least three past verbs and one opinion.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the email frame with gaps and the verb table. Stretch: add a passive description (أُقِيمَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ ...).

lessons.title: Events and exchanges
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I invite, accept, decline and describe events and exchanges?
objectives: Use event and exchange vocabulary
Write invitations and replies
Talk about hosting or visiting an exchange student
successCriteria: All: invite someone to an event
Most: accept or decline politely with a reason
Some: describe an exchange in the past and future
lessons.crossCurricular: MFL and Citizenship: international links; Business: events organisation
lessons.smsc: Moral: hospitality (ḍiyāfa) and welcoming guests; social cohesion
starter: Retrieval: say two things you did on a school trip.
Say 'the trip was useful' in Arabic.
Write a formal greeting in Arabic.

teach.heading: Events and exchanges
teach.note: Check what pupils know about events at their school. Hospitality is central to Islamic and Arab culture, so connect with the host family. The verb اِسْتَضَافَ (to host) is Form X: اِسْتَضَفْنَا طَالِبًا مِنْ مِصْرَ means 'we hosted a student from Egypt'. Practise nouns with a mini-quiz.

teach.heading: Invite, accept, decline

left.title: Inviting and accepting
points: يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ أَدْعُوَكَ إِلَى حُضُورِ حَفْلِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ
I am pleased to invite you to the school concert on Friday

right.title: Declining politely
points: لِلْأَسَفِ لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ الْحُضُورَ لِأَنَّ عِنْدِي دَرْسًا
Unfortunately I cannot attend because I have a lesson

teach.note: Teach all three functions. After يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ the verb is subjunctive (أَدْعُوَ). Accepting: بِكُلِّ سُرُورٍ (with great pleasure). Declining: لِلْأَسَفِ لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ لِأَنَّ ... (unfortunately I cannot because ...), then an alternative. Pupils practise pairs. Remind them: always give a reason when declining; it is both polite and a mark-earning extension.

teach.heading: Model: describing an exchange

model.problem: Say: 'Last year we hosted a student from Egypt. He stayed with my family for two weeks. Next year I will visit him.'
steps: 'Last year we hosted a student from Egypt' = الْعَامَ الْمَاضِيَ اسْتَضَفْنَا طَالِبًا مِنْ مِصْرَ
'He stayed with my family for two weeks' = أَقَامَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي أُسْبُوعَيْنِ
'Next year I will visit him' = الْعَامَ الْقَادِمَ سَأَزُورُهُ
model.answer: الْعَامَ الْمَاضِيَ اسْتَضَفْنَا طَالِبًا مِنْ مِصْرَ. أَقَامَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي أُسْبُوعَيْنِ. الْعَامَ الْقَادِمَ سَأَزُورُهُ.

teach.note: Show how to mix past and future. Note الْعَامَ الْمَاضِيَ and الْعَامَ الْقَادِمَ as accusative time phrases. The future plan uses سَـ with the 'we' form. Pupils write a version about an imaginary exchange with a school in Jordan.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which politely declines an invitation?
options: شُكْرًا، لِلْأَسَفِ لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ لِأَنَّ عِنْدِي دَرْسًا
check.why: It thanks, apologises and gives a reason. A is curt, C accepts, D says 'I am invited'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A is rude; C has the wrong form of 'I cannot'; D is 'I am invited'. Ask pupils which polite phrase they would add.

practice: Invite a friend to a sports day; then accept; then decline with a reason.
Write the Arabic: 'We hosted a student from Jordan.'
Say two sentences about an exchange you would like to take part in.
independent: Core: write an invitation (3 sentences) and a reply (3 sentences).
Extend: add details of date, time and place.
Stretch: write a 100-word email describing an exchange visit and what you plan next.
exit: Write: 'I invite you to the exhibition on Monday.'
Write: 'Unfortunately I cannot come.'
lessons.homework: Write an invitation to a school event (60 words) and a polite reply declining it.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the invitation frame in order (greeting, event, date, place, closing). Stretch: add a conditional (إِذَا سَمَحَ الْوَقْتُ سَأَحْضُرُ).

lessons.unit: Unit 4.1: Using languages beyond the classroom
lessons.title: Languages and friendships: forming relationships and travelling
lessons.bigQuestion: How does knowing a language help me build friendships and travel with confidence?
objectives: Explain how languages build relationships
Use real and unreal conditionals
Describe travelling with language skills
successCriteria: All: say why languages matter for friendships
Most: use إِذَا + past meaning for a real future condition
Some: use لَوْ ... لَـ for an unreal condition
lessons.crossCurricular: MFL, Geography and Citizenship: global communication and cultural awareness
lessons.smsc: Social and cultural: getting to know others (ta'āruf) and respectful dialogue
starter: Retrieval: invite a friend to a school concert.
Say 'I cannot come because I have a lesson'.
Say 'we hosted a student from Egypt'.

teach.heading: Languages and people
teach.note: Pupils discuss languages they and their families speak. Be inclusive: heritage languages and Arabic count. Introduce the nouns and the key verb phrase: تَكْوِينُ صَدَاقَاتٍ (forming friendships), التَّوَاصُلُ مَعَ ... (communicating with ...). Note طَلَاقَةٌ and بِطَلَاقَةٍ (adverbial). Ask: what can you do with Arabic that you could not do before?

teach.heading: If: real and unreal

left.title: Real: إِذَا
points: إِذَا تَعَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا فَسَأَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ أَقَارِبِي
If I learn Arabic well, I will speak with my relatives

right.title: Unreal: لَوْ
points: لَوْ تَعَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ مُنْذُ الصِّغَرِ لَتَحَدَّثْتُ بِطَلَاقَةٍ
If I had learnt Arabic from childhood, I would speak fluently

teach.note: إِذَا + PAST verb describes a possible future situation and the result takes سَـ/سَوْفَ (often with فَ). لَوْ + past describes an unreal or contrary-to-fact condition, and its result has لَـ + past. Note the tense is a past form in both but the meaning is different: pupils must read the particle. A Higher-tier feature: ask pupils to work out the meaning of each. Do not confuse with إِنْ (formal 'if').

teach.heading: Model: Jordan trip

model.problem: Translate: 'If I speak Arabic when I travel to Jordan, I will make new friends.'
steps: 'If I speak Arabic' = إِذَا تَحَدَّثْتُ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ
'when I travel to Jordan' = عِنْدَمَا أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْأُرْدُنِّ
'I will make new friends' = فَسَأُكَوِّنُ صَدَاقَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً
model.answer: إِذَا تَحَدَّثْتُ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ عِنْدَمَا أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْأُرْدُنِّ فَسَأُكَوِّنُ صَدَاقَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً.

teach.note: Model the sentences and the connecting with عِنْدَمَا and إِذَا. The sentence about travel recycles holiday vocabulary and the future. Pupils translate the final answer back into English as a check. Mention that fluent speech links ideas.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'If I study hard, I will succeed'?
check.why: A possible future condition uses إِذَا + past and then سَـ in the result. B is unreal ('if I had studied, I would have succeeded'); D is a past statement.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. B is unreal (would have succeeded); A is a present-tense colloquial construction; D is two plain past statements. Ask which particle makes it a condition.

practice: Complete the real condition: إِذَا سَافَرْتُ إِلَى مِصْرَ ___ (I will practise Arabic).
Say: 'If I had learnt French, I would have travelled to Paris.'
Explain in English the difference between إِذَا and لَوْ.
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about how languages help friendship and travel.
Extend: add one real and one unreal condition.
Stretch: write 100 words on why every pupil should learn a language.
exit: Write: 'If I learn Arabic, I will talk to my grandmother.'
Write one unreal condition about languages.
lessons.homework: Write 80 words on how languages help with friendships and travel, including two conditions.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: provide the two condition templates with blanks. Stretch: add a conditional chain with فَـ ... ثُمَّ ... and a concession بِالرَّغْمِ مِنْ.

lessons.unit: Unit 4.1: Using languages beyond the classroom
lessons.title: Languages in the world of work
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I read and respond to a job advert that asks for languages?
objectives: Read job adverts for languages
Use a relative clause without الَّذِي after an indefinite noun
Write a short application with language skills
successCriteria: All: say which languages you speak and how well
Most: understand and use an indefinite relative clause
Some: write a developed application using several structures
lessons.crossCurricular: Careers and Business: CV and application writing; MFL: translator and interpreter roles
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty about skills; serving others through work
starter: Retrieval: say one real and one unreal condition with إِذَا / لَوْ.
Say 'fluently' and 'forming friendships' in Arabic.
Say 'I will travel to Jordan next year'.

teach.heading: Jobs with languages
teach.note: Pupils guess jobs where languages matter (translator, tour guide, teacher, airline staff). The word مُرْشِدٌ سِيَاحِيٌّ should be familiar from the trip lesson. يُجِيدُ is Form IV: 'is good at, masters'. Pupils say which skills they could list on a CV.

teach.heading: Relative clause after an indefinite noun
teach.note: Key rule: الَّذِي is used only after a DEFINITE noun. After an indefinite noun the relative clause is attached directly, with no pronoun. Pupils practise with pairs of sentences. This matters in adverts (reading and translation) because adverts are full of indefinite nouns: مُوَظَّفٌ يُجِيدُ ...

teach.heading: A practice advert

quote.text: تُعْلِنُ شَرِكَةُ السَّفَرِ عَنْ حَاجَتِهَا إِلَى مُوَظَّفٍ يُجِيدُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ. يُشْتَرَطُ أَنْ تَكُونَ لَدَيْهِ خِبْرَةٌ لَا تَقِلُّ عَنْ سَنَتَيْنِ.
quote.source: Original practice text for this lesson (travel company advert)

teach.note: Original text. Read the advert with pupils and ask them to mark every indefinite relative clause. Questions are in the practice section. The clause لَا تَقِلُّ عَنْ means 'not less than'. Teach the passive يُشْتَرَطُ as 'is required'. Then work out the English together. Reading answers in English must be precise: 'at least two years' not 'two years'.

teach.heading: Model: translating the advert

model.problem: Translate: تُعْلِنُ شَرِكَةُ السَّفَرِ عَنْ حَاجَتِهَا إِلَى مُوَظَّفٍ يُجِيدُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ.
steps: تُعْلِنُ شَرِكَةُ السَّفَرِ = the travel company announces
عَنْ حَاجَتِهَا إِلَى = that it needs (its need for)
مُوَظَّفٍ يُجِيدُ = an employee who is proficient in
الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ = Arabic and English
model.answer: The travel company announces that it needs an employee who is fluent in Arabic and English.

teach.note: Notice the order: what the company needs, then the requirements. The translation should sound natural in English: 'The travel company announces that it needs an employee who is fluent in Arabic and English.' Pupils then translate the second sentence themselves and compare.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'a company that seeks an employee'?
check.why: After an indefinite noun (شَرِكَةٌ) no relative pronoun is used. C is definite and a full sentence ('The company seeks ...'), and A and D wrongly add a pronoun.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A and D use الَّذِي with an indefinite noun; C is a plain sentence. Ask pupils to explain the rule in their own words.

practice: Underline the indefinite relative clauses in: (a) أَبْحَثُ عَنْ وَظِيفَةٍ تَسْمَحُ لِي بِالسَّفَرِ (b) تَطْلُبُ الشَّرِكَةُ مُتَرْجِمَةً تُجِيدُ الْفَرَنْسِيَّةَ
Answer in English: (a) What does the company need? (b) What languages must the employee know? (c) How much experience is needed?
Say which languages you speak and how well.
independent: Core: answer 4 questions in English on the advert.
Extend: translate the second sentence into English.
Stretch: write an application (80 words) for the job.
exit: Translate into English: 'مُتَرْجِمٌ يُجِيدُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ'.
Write one indefinite relative clause in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Write a 70-word letter applying for a job that needs Arabic. Mention languages, experience and one reason you are suitable.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give a glossary of the advert and a two-step translation frame. Stretch: write your own advert using three relative clauses.

lessons.title: Further study and ambitions
lessons.bigQuestion: What do I hope to do after school, and how do I express hopes and intentions?
objectives: Name further-study options
Express intentions with أَنْوِي أَنْ, آمُلُ أَنْ, أَطْمَحُ إِلَى
Explain future plans with reasons
successCriteria: All: say what you want to study next and why
Most: use three verbs of intention with correct structure
Some: write 100 words on your plans with sequencing and conditions
lessons.crossCurricular: Careers and PSHE: post-16 choices; Maths and Science: pathways
lessons.smsc: Spiritual and moral: intention (niyya) and effort (ijtihād); trusting Allah after taking the means
starter: Bismillah. Retrieval: say 'The company seeks an employee who speaks Arabic' in Arabic.
Say 'if I study hard, I will succeed'.
Say the Arabic for 'translator' and 'experience'.

teach.heading: Study options
teach.note: Pupils say what they plan after GCSE: A-levels, college, apprenticeship, university or work. Use the vocabulary list in context. Do not assume a single route: all choices are valid. تَخَصُّصٌ in Arabic is 'specialisation' and is used for a degree subject. Pupils say one subject they would like to study and say it in a full sentence.

teach.heading: Verbs of intention and hope

head: Arabic
Transliteration
Followed by
rows: إِلَى + noun (I aspire to studying medicine)
فِي + noun (I wish to study engineering)

teach.note: Show how each verb connects to its complement: أَنْوِي / آمُلُ / أَتَمَنَّى + أَنْ + subjunctive; أَطْمَحُ إِلَى and أَرْغَبُ فِي + noun or verbal noun (دِرَاسَةِ). Discuss the difference in strength: أَنْوِي (intend) > آمُلُ (hope) > أَتَمَنَّى (wish). The verb أَنْوِي is a defective verb ending in -ī: after أَنْ the first-person subjunctive is أَنْوِيَ. Practise by choosing the correct verb for sentences of different certainty.

teach.heading: Model: my plans

model.problem: Say: 'After I finish my exams, I intend to study medicine at university because I want to help people. I hope to get a scholarship.'
steps: 'After I finish my exams' = بَعْدَ أَنْ أُنْهِيَ امْتِحَانَاتِي
'I intend to study medicine at university' = أَنْوِي أَنْ أَدْرُسَ الطِّبَّ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ
'because I want to help people' = لِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَ النَّاسَ
'I hope to get a scholarship' = آمُلُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى مِنْحَةٍ دِرَاسِيَّةٍ
model.answer: بَعْدَ أَنْ أُنْهِيَ امْتِحَانَاتِي أَنْوِي أَنْ أَدْرُسَ الطِّبَّ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ لِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَ النَّاسَ. آمُلُ أَنْ أَحْصُلَ عَلَى مِنْحَةٍ دِرَاسِيَّةٍ.

teach.note: Model with a clear sequence (after, then, because). Use the pattern بَعْدَ أَنْ + subjunctive (أُنْهِيَ). Highlight the use of three verbs of intention in three sentences. Pupils personalise the model, keeping the structure. Be sensitive to different ambitions and circumstances.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'I hope to get a scholarship'?
check.why: آمُلُ أَنْ + subjunctive (أَحْصُلَ). A keeps the indicative ending, C omits أَنْ, and D combines أَنْ with سَـ.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A keeps the indicative; C omits أَنْ; D has a clash of future and أَنْ. Ask pupils to give the rule.

practice: Say what you intend to study and where, using أَنْوِي أَنْ.
Say what you hope for with آمُلُ أَنْ and one wish with أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ.
Translate: 'I aspire to studying engineering because I like mathematics.'
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about your plans after school.
Extend: add the order of events with بَعْدَ أَنْ and ثُمَّ.
Stretch: write 100 words on two different possible futures, using إِذَا for one.
exit: Write: 'I intend to study at university.'
Write: 'I hope to be a teacher.'
lessons.homework: Write 80 words on what you intend to do after your exams and why.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the verb-of-intention table and a plan frame. Stretch: add a conditional (إِذَا حَصَلْتُ عَلَى ... سَأَدْرُسُ ...) and a contrast with وَإِلَّا.

lessons.title: Volunteering and training
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do people volunteer, and how do I talk about it in different tenses?
objectives: Use volunteering and training vocabulary
Describe volunteering in past, present and future
Explain the benefits of volunteering
successCriteria: All: say you volunteer or would like to volunteer
Most: use the verb تَطَوَّعَ in three tenses
Some: justify the benefits with connected sentences
lessons.crossCurricular: Citizenship and PSHE: community action; Careers: building a CV
lessons.smsc: Moral and spiritual: cooperation in goodness; sadaqa and service to society
starter: Retrieval: say 'I intend to study medicine'.
Say 'I hope to get a scholarship'.
Name three jobs in Arabic.

teach.heading: Volunteering vocabulary
teach.note: Collect pupils' real experience: masjid volunteering, charity events, helping neighbours. Pupils often do this already, so affirm it. Nouns and verbs: تَطَوَّعَ is Form V (to volunteer). Common prepositions: تَطَوَّعَ فِي (volunteer at). Also introduce أُسَاعِدُ كِبَارَ السِّنِّ (I help the elderly).

teach.heading: Past, present, future
teach.note: Pupils practise the three tenses with one verb. The negative past uses لَمْ + jussive: لَمْ أَتَطَوَّعْ. After لَمْ the verb takes a jussive (sukun on the last letter). Drill with other verbs: لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ, لَمْ أَذْهَبْ. Ask pupils to say what they did, do and will do.

teach.heading: An authentic source on cooperation

quote.text: وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى'Help one another in goodness and piety.'

teach.note: Surah al-Ma'idah 5:2, part of the verse. Pupils annotate the verb (تَعَاوَنُوا: imperative plural, 'cooperate') and the two nouns (الْبِرِّ goodness, التَّقْوَى piety). Link it to the imperative from Year 10. Teacher: check the wording against a mushaf before display. Connect to volunteering as a lived application.

teach.heading: Model: volunteering experience

model.problem: Say: 'Last year I volunteered at a food bank. I learnt new skills and met kind people. This year I will join a first-aid course.'
steps: 'Last year I volunteered at a food bank' = الْعَامَ الْمَاضِيَ تَطَوَّعْتُ فِي بَنْكِ الطَّعَامِ
'I learnt new skills' = تَعَلَّمْتُ مَهَارَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً
'and met kind people' = وَالْتَقَيْتُ بِأُنَاسٍ طَيِّبِينَ
'This year I will join a first-aid course' = هَذَا الْعَامَ سَأَلْتَحِقُ بِدَوْرَةٍ تَدْرِيبِيَّةٍ فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ
model.answer: الْعَامَ الْمَاضِيَ تَطَوَّعْتُ فِي بَنْكِ الطَّعَامِ. تَعَلَّمْتُ مَهَارَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً وَالْتَقَيْتُ بِأُنَاسٍ طَيِّبِينَ. هَذَا الْعَامَ سَأَلْتَحِقُ بِدَوْرَةٍ تَدْرِيبِيَّةٍ فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ.

teach.note: Model the three tenses in one paragraph. Highlight the connectors (وَ, ثُمَّ) and the benefits (skills, friends). Pupils then write their own. Use this as a template for the 'future' answer in the conversation.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'I volunteer at a charity'?
check.why: The present tense أَتَطَوَّعُ has no tense marker. The others are past, future and past negative.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A is past, C is future, D is a past negative. Ask pupils to circle the tense marker.

practice: Say one thing you did, do and will do to help others.
Write: 'I have not volunteered before, but I will volunteer next year.'
Name two benefits of volunteering in Arabic.
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about volunteering in the three tenses.
Extend: add benefits and a reason.
Stretch: write 100 words persuading a friend to volunteer.
exit: Write: 'I volunteered at the masjid last Ramadan.'
Write: 'Volunteering gives me new skills.'
lessons.homework: Write 80 words about volunteering or training you have done or would like to do.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the tense table with a sentence frame per tense. Stretch: add a relative clause (جَمْعِيَّةٌ تُسَاعِدُ الْفُقَرَاءَ).

lessons.title: Jobs and professions
lessons.bigQuestion: What job would I like, and how do I explain my choice?
objectives: Name jobs with masculine and feminine forms
Say what job you want and why
Describe family members' jobs
successCriteria: All: name five jobs and say your parents' jobs
Most: use أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ + accusative noun correctly
Some: give two reasons and compare two careers
lessons.crossCurricular: Careers: sectors and professions; Science: STEM careers
lessons.smsc: Moral: dignity of all honest work (kasb ḥalāl) and serving the community
starter: Retrieval: say 'I volunteer at a charity' and 'I will volunteer'.
Say 'I intend to study at university'.
Name three school subjects.

teach.heading: Jobs
teach.note: Teach with feminine pairs. Feminine forms mostly add ة; note مُحَامٍ (a defective noun) becomes مُحَامِيَةٌ. Practise by showing pictures and asking 'what is his/her job?' Use the neutral mention of both genders to avoid stereotypes; point out that all pupils can aim for any career.

teach.heading: Saying what job I want
bullets: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا
I want to be a doctor
أُمِّي مُمَرِّضَةٌ وَأَبِي مُهَنْدِسٌ
My mother is a nurse and my father is an engineer
أُرِيدُ هَذِهِ الْمِهْنَةَ لِأَنَّهَا تُفِيدُ النَّاسَ
I want this job because it benefits people
teach.note: Teach أَنْ أَكُونَ + accusative predicate: the job after 'to be' takes -an (طَبِيبًا) because it is the predicate of an accusative-governed verb. Contrast with the present sentence: أُمِّي مُمَرِّضَةٌ (no verb, nominative). Elicit reasons using يُفِيدُ النَّاسَ, أَجْرٌ جَيِّدٌ (good pay), أُحِبُّ الْعِلْمَ.

teach.heading: The predicate after 'to be'

misconception.right: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا - the job after 'to be' takes tanween fatha

teach.note: A very frequent error. Ask pupils to say why: كَانَ and أَنْ أَكُونَ are 'sisters of kāna', and the predicate is accusative. Drill with five different jobs on mini-whiteboards.

teach.heading: Model: dream job and family jobs

model.problem: Say: 'I want to be a doctor because I want to help people. My mother is a nurse and my father is an engineer.'
steps: 'I want to be a doctor' = أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا
'because I want to help people' = لِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَ النَّاسَ
'My mother is a nurse' = أُمِّي مُمَرِّضَةٌ
'and my father is an engineer' = وَأَبِي مُهَنْدِسٌ
model.answer: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا لِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَ النَّاسَ. أُمِّي مُمَرِّضَةٌ وَأَبِي مُهَنْدِسٌ.

teach.note: Model with a mix of present nominal sentences (family) and a want-structure (me). Pupils record themselves. Highlight the reason clause. Encourage pupils to add a past or future detail, e.g. what they have already done to move towards the career.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'My mother is a lawyer'?
check.why: The feminine of مُحَامٍ is مُحَامِيَةٌ. A is masculine, C is not a word, D is a plural.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A is the masculine form; C is a wrong ending; D is plural. Ask pupils to say the feminine pattern.

practice: Say the jobs of three family members.
Say what you want to be and give two reasons.
Translate: 'My sister wants to be an engineer because she likes mathematics.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about jobs (family and yours).
Extend: add a comparison of two jobs (أَصْعَبُ مِنْ).
Stretch: write 100 words on the career you want, why, and the steps to reach it.
exit: Write: 'My brother is a teacher.'
Write: 'I want to be a pilot.' (pilot = طَيَّارٌ)
lessons.homework: Write 80 words on the job you would like and the job you would not like, with reasons.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the job table with images and the frame أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ ___ لِأَنَّ___. Stretch: add the future (سَأَدْرُسُ ... لِكَيْ أَصِيرَ ... so that I become ...).

lessons.title: Careers: applications, interviews and part-time work
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I apply for a job and speak about work?
objectives: Use work and career vocabulary
Write a short application with a CV mention
Answer interview questions politely
successCriteria: All: say whether you want full-time or part-time work
Most: use الْمُؤَهِّلَات and خِبْرَة in a formal sentence
Some: write a 90-word application and answer four interview questions
lessons.crossCurricular: Careers and Business: CV writing; English: formal writing
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty, reliability (amāna) and professional manners
starter: Retrieval: say 'I want to be a nurse'.
Give the feminine of مُعَلِّمٌ and مُهَنْدِسٌ.
Say 'my father is an accountant'.

teach.heading: The world of work
teach.note: Pupils say where they might work. Introduce the vocabulary. Note the idafa pairs: دَوَامٌ كَامِلٌ / جُزْئِيٌّ use adjectives; سَاعَاتُ الْعَمَلِ is an idafa. Many pupils have a part-time job or will have: use real experience. Pupils compare full-time with part-time.

teach.heading: Interview questions
bullets: لِمَاذَا تُرِيدُ هَذِهِ الْوَظِيفَةَ؟
Why do you want this job?
مَا هِيَ مُؤَهِّلَاتُكَ؟
What are your qualifications?
هَلْ لَدَيْكَ خِبْرَةٌ؟
Do you have experience?
لَدَيَّ خِبْرَةٌ فِي الْعَمَلِ مَعَ النَّاسِ
I have experience working with people
teach.note: Teach 'to have' with لَدَى: لَدَيَّ (I have), لَدَيْكَ (you have), لَدَيْهِ (he has). Practise interview role plays in pairs. For the speaking exam, 'Work' may be one of the conversation themes. Remind pupils to answer in full sentences with a reason.

teach.heading: A formal application

model.problem: Write: 'I am applying for the post of accountant in your company. I have two years of experience and I speak Arabic and English. I attach my CV.'
steps: 'I am applying for the post of accountant' = أَتَقَدَّمُ لِوَظِيفَةِ مُحَاسِبٍ فِي شَرِكَتِكُمْ
'I have two years of experience' = لَدَيَّ خِبْرَةٌ لِمُدَّةِ سَنَتَيْنِ
'and I speak Arabic and English' = وَأَتَحَدَّثُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ
'I attach my CV' = أَرْفَقْتُ سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّةَ
model.answer: أَتَقَدَّمُ لِوَظِيفَةِ مُحَاسِبٍ فِي شَرِكَتِكُمْ. لَدَيَّ خِبْرَةٌ لِمُدَّةِ سَنَتَيْنِ وَأَتَحَدَّثُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ. أَرْفَقْتُ سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّةَ.

teach.note: Show the formal register. Mark the phrases: أَتَقَدَّمُ لِوَظِيفَةِ (I apply for the post of), لَدَيَّ خِبْرَةٌ (I have experience), أَرْفَقْتُ (I attach). Pupils underline them. After that, pupils copy the structure and put in their own details. Note the genitive after وَظِيفَةِ: وَظِيفَةِ مُحَاسِبٍ.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'part-time work'?
check.why: دَوَامٌ جُزْئِيٌّ is part-time. A is full-time, B is a monthly salary, D is a personal interview.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. The distractors are other work words. Ask pupils to make a sentence with the correct answer.

practice: Answer the four interview questions in Arabic in pairs.
Write the Arabic: 'I work part-time in a shop.'
Say one advantage and one disadvantage of part-time work.
independent: Core: write a short application (4 sentences).
Extend: add your languages and a reason you are suitable.
Stretch: write a 100-word letter applying for a job, with a formal opening and closing.
exit: Write: 'I have experience in teaching.'
Write: 'Why do you want this job?'
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word application for a job you would like. Use لَدَيَّ and أَتَقَدَّمُ لِ.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the application frame with gaps. Stretch: add a conditional promise (إِذَا قُبِلْتُ سَأَعْمَلُ بِجِدٍّ ...).

lessons.title: Sports and international events that bring the world together
lessons.bigQuestion: How do global events help people from different countries come together?
objectives: Describe sports and international events
Give years correctly
Express advantages and disadvantages of global events
successCriteria: All: name a global event and say what it is
Most: say a year correctly and use the past tense in a short account
Some: weigh up the benefits and costs of hosting a global event
lessons.crossCurricular: PE: global sports; Geography: host countries and tourism
lessons.smsc: Social and cultural: getting to know others (ta'āruf), fair play and respect
starter: Retrieval: say 'I applied for the job of teacher' (formal).
Say 'part-time' and 'salary' in Arabic.
Say 'I want to be a pilot'.

teach.heading: Event vocabulary
teach.note: Pupils name an event they have followed. Link to PE and Geography. Exam vocabulary to recognise only: مِهْرَجَانٌ مُوسِيقِيٌّ (music festival) and حَفْلَةٌ مُوسِيقِيَّةٌ (concert) can appear in exam texts; pupils write about sports, book fairs and cultural events. Highlight the plural: لَاعِبٌ → لَاعِبُونَ (players, sound masculine plural); الْأَلْعَابُ الْأُولِمْبِيَّةُ is plural because 'games' (أَلْعَابٌ). Pupils say a sentence about their favourite team or event with an opinion.

teach.heading: Saying the year
teach.note: Years use the word عَامَ (accusative of time) and the full number: thousand then units then tens. The dual of thousand is أَلْفَيْنِ (accusative). Pupils say the years aloud, then write them. Note: in the exam, years appear as digits when heard; but in reading and writing the words are needed to be recognised. Practise with dates the pupils know (the year of the last World Cup).

teach.heading: Benefits and costs

left.title: Benefits
points: تَجْمَعُ الْأَحْدَاثُ الرِّيَاضِيَّةُ النَّاسَ مِنْ دُوَلٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ
Sports events bring people from different countries together

teach.note: Ask pupils to categorise each statement. Then add one of their own. Use مِنْ مَزَايَا and مِنْ عُيُوبِ. Challenge: write a sentence that combines both with بَيْنَمَا or وَلَكِنْ. This is the type of evaluation that the speaking conversation and writing tasks reward.

teach.heading: Model: an event account

model.problem: Say: 'Sports events bring people together. Qatar hosted the World Cup in 2022. I watched the final with my family and it was exciting.'
steps: 'Sports events bring people together' = تَجْمَعُ الْأَحْدَاثُ الرِّيَاضِيَّةُ النَّاسَ
'Qatar hosted the World Cup in 2022' = اِسْتَضَافَتْ قَطَرُ كَأْسَ الْعَالَمِ عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَاثْنَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ
'I watched the final with my family' = شَاهَدْتُ الْمُبَارَاةَ النِّهَائِيَّةَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي
'and it was exciting' = وَكَانَتْ مُثِيرَةً
model.answer: تَجْمَعُ الْأَحْدَاثُ الرِّيَاضِيَّةُ النَّاسَ. اِسْتَضَافَتْ قَطَرُ كَأْسَ الْعَالَمِ عَامَ أَلْفَيْنِ وَاثْنَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ. شَاهَدْتُ الْمُبَارَاةَ النِّهَائِيَّةَ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي وَكَانَتْ مُثِيرَةً.

teach.note: Show the structure: general statement, specific event with the year, personal experience, opinion. Notice اِسْتَضَافَتْ with a feminine subject (قَطَرُ). Pupils write a version with their own event.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'in the year 2022'?
check.why: Accusative of time: عَامَ with أَلْفَيْنِ وَاثْنَيْنِ وَعِشْرِينَ (dual and tens in the accusative). A uses nominative endings, C omits 'two', D is 2030.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A has the wrong case and a nominative number; C skips the 'two' unit; D is a different year. Ask pupils to say why the dual ending is used.

practice: Say three global events and one fact about each.
Write the years 2000 and 2030 in words.
Say one benefit and one cost of hosting the Olympics.
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about a sports or international event.
Extend: add the year in words and a past-tense experience.
Stretch: write 100 words evaluating the benefits and costs of hosting a major event.
exit: Write: 'The match was exciting and the fans were happy.'
Write the year 2022 in words.
lessons.homework: Write 80 words about a global sports or international event you know. Include a year and one opinion.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the year-formation card and event vocabulary. Stretch: use the passive (أُقِيمَ ... was held) and a contrast with وَلَكِنْ.

lessons.title: Campaigns and good causes
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I help others through campaigns and charity, and how do I persuade people?
objectives: Use campaign and charity vocabulary
Use plural imperatives to persuade
Write a short campaign poster and report
successCriteria: All: name a cause and say what you do to help
Most: use plural imperatives (تَبَرَّعُوا) to persuade
Some: write a developed campaign text with past and future
lessons.crossCurricular: Citizenship and PSHE: charity and global issues; English: persuasive writing
lessons.smsc: Moral: charity (ṣadaqa), mercy and standing with the vulnerable
starter: Retrieval: say '2022' in words.
Say 'sports events bring people together'.
Say 'the match was exciting'.

teach.heading: Causes and campaigns
teach.note: Pupils name causes they care about (hunger, refugees, education, the environment). Introduce the vocabulary. Notice nouns of cause: الْفَقْرُ (poverty), الْجُوعُ (hunger). Explain ṣadaqa and zakat connections respectfully: voluntary charity and obligatory alms. Ask what the school or community has done.

teach.heading: Persuading with imperatives
bullets: اِنْضَمُّوا إِلَى حَمْلَتِنَا!
Join our campaign!
تَبَرَّعُوا بِمَا تَسْتَطِيعُونَ
Donate what you can
سَاعِدُوا اللَّاجِئِينَ
Help the refugees
teach.note: Recall the imperative from the directions lesson: plural -ū (with a silent alif). Notice that the verb is Form VII (اِنْضَمُّوا) or Form V (تَبَرَّعُوا): the pattern still works. A poster uses the imperative plural to address a group. Write a heading and three imperatives; add one reason (لِأَنَّ ...). Mention the persuasive device of repetition.

teach.heading: Model: reporting a campaign

model.problem: Write: 'Our school organised a campaign to collect donations for refugees. We raised a lot of money and we will repeat it next year.'
steps: 'Our school organised a campaign' = نَظَّمَتْ مَدْرَسَتُنَا حَمْلَةً
'to collect donations for refugees' = لِجَمْعِ التَّبَرُّعَاتِ لِلَّاجِئِينَ
'We raised a lot of money' = جَمَعْنَا مَبْلَغًا كَبِيرًا
'and we will repeat it next year' = وَسَنُكَرِّرُهَا الْعَامَ الْقَادِمَ
model.answer: نَظَّمَتْ مَدْرَسَتُنَا حَمْلَةً لِجَمْعِ التَّبَرُّعَاتِ لِلَّاجِئِينَ. جَمَعْنَا مَبْلَغًا كَبِيرًا وَسَنُكَرِّرُهَا الْعَامَ الْقَادِمَ.

teach.note: Model the past report. Notice the verb-subject order with a feminine subject (نَظَّمَتْ مَدْرَسَتُنَا) and the verbal noun after لِ (لِجَمْعِ التَّبَرُّعَاتِ). Then pupils write their own campaign report with the details changed.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which tells a GROUP: 'Donate to the campaign'?
check.why: The imperative for a group ends in -ū. A is for one man, C is a negative past, D is a statement in the present.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A is to one man, C is a negative past, D is present. Ask pupils how to say it to a woman.

practice: Say three imperatives for a campaign poster.
Translate: 'We donated money to the charity.'
Say what cause you care about and why.
independent: Core: write a poster with a title and three imperatives.
Extend: add a report in the past tense.
Stretch: write 100 words persuading people to join a campaign, with a plan for the future.
exit: Write: 'Join us to help the poor.'
Write: 'Our school organised a charity day.'
lessons.homework: Write 80 words promoting a campaign for a cause you care about. Use two plural imperatives.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the poster frame with imperative bank. Stretch: add the negative imperative (لَا تَنْسَوْا Do not forget) and a condition.

lessons.title: Being green: what we can do
lessons.bigQuestion: What can each of us do to protect the environment?
objectives: Use environment vocabulary
Use obligation and negative imperatives
Explain what you do and will do to be green
successCriteria: All: name three green actions
Most: use يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ and a negative imperative accurately
Some: write a developed answer using present, future and a reason
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography and Science: pollution, recycling and sustainability
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: stewardship of the earth (amāna) and avoiding waste (isrāf)
starter: Retrieval: say 'Join our campaign' to a group.
Say 'Donate what you can'.
Say 'we must arrive on time'.

teach.heading: Green vocabulary
teach.note: Link to the Geography unit on sustainability. Pupils say what they do at home. أُعِيدُ تَدْوِيرَ ... (I recycle) uses the Form IV verb أَعَادَ, which also means 'I return'. Drill with the noun phrase and a verb. Emphasise إِعَادَةُ التَّدْوِيرِ as an idafa: the first noun has no article.

teach.heading: Obligation and prohibition

left.title: We must ...
points: يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نُعِيدَ تَدْوِيرَ الْبَلَاسْتِيكِ

right.title: Do not ... (to a group)
points: Do not throw rubbish in the street

teach.note: Use the structures from the school rules lesson. Add the negative plural imperative: لَا + jussive: لَا تَرْمُوا (the final nun drops). Prepare pupils to write a leaflet. Mention the Islamic ethos of stewardship; the Qur'an warns against wastefulness (isrāf).

teach.heading: An authentic source

quote.text: وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا'Eat and drink, and do not be wasteful.'

teach.note: Surah al-A'raf 7:31, part of the verse about eating and drinking without wastefulness. Teacher: check the wording against a mushaf before display. Pupils parse the imperatives (كُلُوا, اشْرَبُوا) and the negative (وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا). Link it to wasting water, food and energy.

teach.heading: Model: what I do and will do

model.problem: Say: 'I always recycle plastic and I use public transport. In the future I will plant trees. We must protect the environment because it is a trust.'
steps: 'I always recycle plastic' = أُعِيدُ تَدْوِيرَ الْبَلَاسْتِيكِ دَائِمًا
'and I use public transport' = وَأَسْتَخْدِمُ وَسَائِلَ النَّقْلِ الْعَامَّةِ
'In the future I will plant trees' = فِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ سَأَزْرَعُ الْأَشْجَارَ
'We must protect the environment because it is a trust' = يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَحْمِيَ الْبِيئَةَ لِأَنَّهَا أَمَانَةٌ
model.answer: أُعِيدُ تَدْوِيرَ الْبَلَاسْتِيكِ دَائِمًا وَأَسْتَخْدِمُ وَسَائِلَ النَّقْلِ الْعَامَّةِ. فِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ سَأَزْرَعُ الْأَشْجَارَ. يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَحْمِيَ الْبِيئَةَ لِأَنَّهَا أَمَانَةٌ.

teach.note: Model the present, future and obligation. Highlight the 'because it is a trust' reason. Pupils then say it with their own actions. Stress giving a real reason, not just a list.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'Do not throw rubbish' (to a group)?
check.why: Negative command to a group = لَا + jussive plural (-ū). A is for one man, C wrongly uses the imperative after لَا, D is a negative past.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A is for one man, C has the wrong form of the command, D is a past negative. Ask pupils to say the group form of the positive command.

practice: Say three things you do to help the environment.
Say two things we must do and one thing we must not do.
Translate: 'Pollution is a big problem and we must protect the planet.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences on being green.
Extend: add obligations and a negative command.
Stretch: write 100 words persuading a friend to be green, with a reason and a future plan.
exit: Write: 'I save water because it is precious.'
Write: 'Do not waste food.' (to a group)
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word leaflet with a title, three commands (positive and negative) and one reason.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the vocabulary list with pictures and the frame أَنَا ___ دَائِمًا. Stretch: use a conditional (إِذَا لَمْ نَحْمِ الْبِيئَةَ فَسَتَزْدَادُ ...) with a result.

lessons.title: Access to natural resources
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do some people lack water and energy, and what can be done?
objectives: Use resource and climate vocabulary
Link causes and effects with connectors
Read and translate a short article on water
successCriteria: All: name three natural resources and one problem
Most: use بِسَبَبِ and لِذَلِكَ accurately
Some: read and translate an article and write a cause-effect paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: resource management and climate change; Science: energy sources
lessons.smsc: Moral: justice (ʿadl) in sharing resources; gratitude for water and provisions
starter: Retrieval: say 'Do not waste water' to a group.
Say 'I recycle plastic and save water'.
Say 'we must protect the environment because it is a trust'.

teach.heading: Resources and problems
teach.note: Pupils say which resources they use daily. Teach the problem words and how they link. Focus on the idafa structures: نَقْصُ الْمِيَاهِ (shortage of water), الطَّاقَةُ الْمُتَجَدِّدَةُ (renewable energy). Introduce إِنَّ: إِنَّ الْمَاءَ نِعْمَةٌ (Indeed water is a blessing), with the noun after إِنَّ in the accusative.

teach.heading: Linking cause and effect
teach.note: Explain the four connectors: بِسَبَبِ + noun in the genitive; لِأَنَّ + sentence (subject accusative); نَتِيجَةً لِ + noun; لِذَلِكَ + sentence ('therefore'). These help build developed answers in both the writing paper and the speaking conversation. Elicit one sentence for each from pupils with the same problem.

teach.heading: A practice text

quote.text: يَعِيشُ مَلَايِينُ النَّاسِ فِي مَنَاطِقَ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهَا الْمِيَاهُ النَّظِيفَةُ. تُنَفِّذُ جَمْعِيَّاتٌ خَيْرِيَّةٌ مَشْرُوعَاتٍ لِحَفْرِ الْآبَارِ وَبِنَاءِ مَحَطَّاتِ التَّنْقِيَةِ، وَيَتَطَوَّعُ الشَّبَابُ لِلْمُسَاعَدَةِ.
quote.source: Original practice text for this lesson (water access)

teach.note: Original text. Pupils read it and answer in English. Draw attention to the passive-like meaning and the idafa structures: مَحَطَّاتِ التَّنْقِيَةِ (purification stations), حَفْرِ الْآبَارِ (digging wells). Pupils annotate the verb and subject of each sentence before translating. Discuss accuracy in the translation: every detail should be rendered.

teach.heading: Model: translating the text

model.problem: Translate the first sentence: يَعِيشُ مَلَايِينُ النَّاسِ فِي مَنَاطِقَ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهَا الْمِيَاهُ النَّظِيفَةُ.
steps: يَعِيشُ مَلَايِينُ النَّاسِ = millions of people live
فِي مَنَاطِقَ = in areas
لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهَا = that (it) does not reach (to them)
الْمِيَاهُ النَّظِيفَةُ = clean water
model.answer: Millions of people live in areas that clean water does not reach.

teach.note: Translate it in chunks, as the translation section requires. Notice that the relative clause لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهَا الْمِيَاهُ attaches directly to the indefinite noun مَنَاطِقَ with a pronoun that points back (إِلَيْهَا). This is a typical Higher-tier structure. The final English must read naturally.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'because of pollution'?
check.why: بِسَبَبِ is followed by a noun in the genitive. A has the wrong case after لِأَنَّ, B has a nominative noun, D is not a valid structure.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. B has the wrong case after بِسَبَبِ; C wrongly uses لِذَلِكَ; D is the wrong connector. Ask pupils to give the rule for the noun that follows بِسَبَبِ.

practice: Answer in English: (a) How many people live without clean water? (b) What do charities build? (c) Who volunteers?
Make cause-effect sentences with بِسَبَبِ and لِذَلِكَ about drought.
Say one way to save energy and one way to save water.
independent: Core: write 5 cause-and-effect sentences on resources.
Extend: translate the second sentence of the practice text.
Stretch: write 100 words on how we can share natural resources fairly.
exit: Translate: 'Water is a blessing.'
Write: 'Because of the drought there is a water shortage.'
lessons.homework: Write 90 words explaining one resource problem, its cause and one solution. Use بِسَبَبِ, لِذَلِكَ and إِنَّ.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give a glossary of the text and the connector table. Stretch: add a passive description (يُسْتَخْدَمُ الْمَاءُ فِي ...) and a condition with إِذَا.

lessons.unit: Exam skills: Papers 1 to 4 (all five themes)
lessons.title: Reading Paper: translating Arabic into English
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I turn Arabic into accurate, natural English without a dictionary?
objectives: Break a text into chunks and identify verbs, subjects and tenses
Handle common Arabic structures in English
Translate a short passage accurately
successCriteria: All: translate simple sentences with the main ideas correct
Most: translate with correct tenses and no omissions
Some: translate relative clauses, the passive and verb-first sentences naturally
lessons.crossCurricular: English: translation and grammatical terminology; MFL: literal versus natural translation
lessons.smsc: Cultural: respect for meaning and accuracy (amāna) when conveying another's words
starter: Retrieval: give the English for 'بِسَبَبِ الْجَفَافِ' and 'لِذَلِكَ'.
Translate: 'مُوَظَّفٌ يُجِيدُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ'.
Say the root of 'مَكْتَبَةٌ'.

teach.heading: The method
bullets: Read the whole text first for the gist
Split into chunks at the verbs
Identify tense, subject and object
Write natural English, then check nothing is missing
teach.note: Paper 3 ends with a translation from Arabic into English (Section C per the spec file). Marks reward accurate content, so the order is meaning first, style second. Emphasise: no dictionaries; use roots and context for unknown words; never leave a gap, write the best guess. Remind pupils that each small word (negation, a preposition, a time word) can carry a mark.

teach.heading: Arabic structure to English

head: Arabic structure
Example
English handling
rows: The students went (verb stays singular in Arabic)
the girls' school / the school of the girls
an employee who is fluent in Arabic
I have been studying Arabic for two years
he used to go on foot

teach.note: Go through each row with a quick example and ask pupils to translate it. These are the structures that most often cause mistranslation. Insist that pupils say the Arabic structure aloud before translating. Pupils add one more example of each from their notes.

teach.heading: A practice passage

quote.text: ذَهَبَتْ مَدْرَسَتُنَا فِي رِحْلَةٍ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ. زُرْنَا الْمَكْتَبَةَ الْكَبِيرَةَ وَتَنَاوَلْنَا الْغَدَاءَ عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ. كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا وَلَكِنَّ الْمَطَرَ سَقَطَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ، لِذَلِكَ عُدْنَا مُبَكِّرِينَ.
quote.source: Original practice passage for this lesson

teach.note: Original passage. Pupils first underline the verbs and say the tense of each. Then they translate in chunks. Check difficult words: عُدْنَا (we returned), مُبَكِّرِينَ (early, plural), الْمَطَرَ (the rain). Prompt: how would an examiner know you understood وَلَكِنَّ (but)? Collect first translations and compare.

teach.heading: Model: translating step by step

model.problem: Translate: ذَهَبَتْ مَدْرَسَتُنَا فِي رِحْلَةٍ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ. زُرْنَا الْمَكْتَبَةَ الْكَبِيرَةَ وَتَنَاوَلْنَا الْغَدَاءَ عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ.
steps: ذَهَبَتْ مَدْرَسَتُنَا فِي رِحْلَةٍ = our school went on a trip
إِلَى مَدِينَةِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ = to the city of Alexandria
زُرْنَا الْمَكْتَبَةَ الْكَبِيرَةَ = we visited the large library
وَتَنَاوَلْنَا الْغَدَاءَ عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ = and we had lunch on the beach
model.answer: Our school went on a trip to the city of Alexandria. We visited the large library and had lunch on the beach.

teach.note: Think aloud with the first two sentences. Notice the decisions: 'went on a trip' not 'went in a trip'; the idafa مَدِينَةِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ becomes 'the city of Alexandria' or simply 'Alexandria'. Pupils do the last sentence themselves on whiteboards.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Best translation of: تَطْلُبُ الشَّرِكَةُ مُوَظَّفًا يُجِيدُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ
options: The company asks an employee who is excellent at Arabic
The company is looking for an employee who is fluent in Arabic
The company employee is fluent in Arabic
The company has an employee and he speaks Arabic
check.why: تَطْلُبُ here means 'seeks'; مُوَظَّفًا يُجِيدُ is an indefinite noun with a relative clause: 'an employee who is fluent in'. The others misread the verb or the relative clause.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A mistranslates the relative clause; C misses the verb; D mistakes the meaning of the verb. Ask pupils to circle the word that gives 'is looking for'.

practice: Underline the verb in each sentence of the passage and say its tense.
Translate the last sentence of the passage: كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا وَلَكِنَّ الْمَطَرَ سَقَطَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ، لِذَلِكَ عُدْنَا مُبَكِّرِينَ.
Translate: 'مَنَحَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ الطَّالِبَ جَائِزَةً' and 'لَمْ أَزُرْ مِصْرَ مِنْ قَبْلُ'.
independent: Core: translate the passage into English.
Extend: translate your own Arabic paragraph from last term into English and compare.
Stretch: write two sentences that trap the translator (e.g. with an idafa and a passive) and give them to a partner.
exit: Translate: 'يَجْمَعُ الْمِهْرَجَانُ النَّاسَ مِنْ دُوَلٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ'.
Name two structures that need careful handling in translation.
lessons.homework: Translate 40 words of Arabic from a past text into English and highlight each structure you found difficult.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the passage with a glossary of 5 words and the first sentence translated. Stretch: translate a passage containing a passive and a conditional with no help.

lessons.title: Extended writing: planning, range and accuracy
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I plan and write an extended piece that scores in the top bands?
objectives: To understand how to plan, write and check an extended Arabic piece that covers every bullet point with range and accuracy
successCriteria: All: cover every bullet point in the task
Most: include three time frames, opinions with reasons and connectives
Some: check accuracy with a checklist and improve one paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: English: planning extended writing (4EB1 Section B and C)
lessons.smsc: Moral: perseverance (sabr) in redrafting work

hook.text: Two pupils write 150 words. One scores far higher. Without reading them, what might the difference be?
hook.a: Covering all bullet points, range of structures, accuracy and organisation.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, Allah loves those who do good with excellence (al-muhsinin)' (al-Baqarah 2:195). We plan and check our writing with the same care.

starter.q: Bismillah. Predicate of كَانَ is: A) مَنْصُوب B) مَرْفُوع

teach.heading: Plan in two minutes

timeline.text: Add: opinion, reason, connective, time frame

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. 1AA0 Paper 4 and 4AA1 Paper 2 both reward covering every bullet point; check word counts in the specifications. Model the plan for the task: اُكْتُبْ مَقَالًا عَنْ حَمْلَةٍ خَيْرِيَّةٍ فِي مَدْرَسَتِكَ.

teach.heading: Model: one developed paragraph

model.problem: Bullet: what you did for the charity campaign.
steps: فِي الشَّهْرِ المَاضِي نَظَّمْنَا حَمْلَةً لِجَمْعِ التَّبَرُّعَاتِ لِلْمُحْتَاجِينَ.
بِعْتُ الكَعْكَ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي، وَجَمَعْنَا مِئَتَيْ جُنَيْهٍ.
كَانَتْ تَجْرِبَةً رَائِعَةً لِأَنَّنَا سَاعَدْنَا غَيْرَنَا.
فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ سَأُشَارِكُ فِي حَمَلَاتٍ أُخْرَى إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.
model.answer: Past narrative, detail with a number, opinion and reason, future

teach.note: Spec 5.1 campaigns and good causes; Islamic link to sadaqah.

teach.heading: Accuracy checklist
bullets: Agreement: gender, number, dual; non-human plurals
Verb forms: person, tense; أَنْ + fathah
Cases after كَانَ، إِنَّ، prepositions; numbers
teach.note: Pupils keep this list for every piece.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which error is in: الحَمَلَاتُ مُفِيدُونَ?
check.why: Non-human plural takes feminine singular: الحَمَلَاتُ مُفِيدَةٌ.

practice.q: Correct: يَجِبُ أَنْ نُسَاعِدُ الفُقَرَاءِ.
practice.a: يَجِبُ أَنْ نُسَاعِدَ الفُقَرَاءَ.
practice.model:
After أَنْ the verb takes fathah: نُسَاعِدَ.
الفُقَرَاء is the object: fathah (الفُقَرَاءَ).

practice.q: Write a conclusion sentence for a charity article.
practice.a: For example: فِي الخِتَامِ، أَنْصَحُ كُلَّ الطُّلَّابِ أَنْ يُشَارِكُوا فِي العَمَلِ الخَيْرِيِّ.

independent.q: Core (portal response box, timed 20 min): اُكْتُبْ مَقَالًا عَنْ حَمْلَةٍ خَيْرِيَّةٍ فِي مَدْرَسَتِكَ: what the campaign was; what you did; why good causes matter; what you will do next. Group B 100 to 130 words; Group A 150 words.
independent.a: Marked with the 1AA0 Paper 4 or 4AA1 Paper 2 style criteria: content, range, accuracy, organisation.
independent.model: Teacher writes the plan on screen and the first sentence.

independent.q: Extend: Use the checklist to correct three errors in your own piece.
independent.a: Three corrected errors, each labelled with its rule

independent.q: Stretch: Add a sentence with إِنَّ and one with لَيْسَ, correctly marked.
independent.a: For example: إِنَّ العَمَلَ الخَيْرِيَّ مُهِمٌّ. لَيْسَ الأَمْرُ صَعْبًا.

exit.q: What is مَقَال? A) article B) plan C) checklist
Big question: what makes extended writing score highly?
exit.a: All bullets covered, range of structures and time frames, accuracy checked, clear organisation.

lessons.homework: Draft 2 of today's article after marking, with every checklist error corrected.
lessons.send: SEND: paragraph frames per bullet. EAL: vocabulary bank for 5.1. Stretch: 250 words with a counter-argument.

School's 1AA0 Speaking and Writing revision booklet (Draft 1, teacher marking, Draft 2) (Group B): writing tasks
Writing checklist (portal worksheet)

lessons.title: Speaking: the conversation and unexpected questions
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I keep talking well when I am asked a question I did not expect?
objectives: To understand how to develop conversation answers and handle unexpected questions in the 1AA0 speaking test
successCriteria: All: answer Theme 1 questions with three developed sentences
Most: use repair phrases to buy time and ask for repetition
Some: answer an unexpected question using a prepared structure bank
lessons.crossCurricular: English: spoken language and active listening
lessons.smsc: Social: confident, polite conversation

hook.text: In a conversation in English, what do you say when you need a second to think? Could the same trick work in Arabic?
hook.a: Yes: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ، بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي ... buy time naturally.

islamicLink.text: Musa (peace be upon him) asked Allah: 'Untie the knot from my tongue so they may understand my speech' (Ta Ha 20:27-28). We can make this du'a before speaking tests.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Let me think': A) دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ B) لَا أَعْرِفُ
'When I was young I used to read' in Arabic?
Name three question words in Arabic.

teach.heading: The conversation task
bullets: Pupil chooses the first theme; the teacher-examiner chooses the second
Questions are not given in advance
Marks for communication, range, accuracy and spontaneity
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Check the current 1AA0 specification and the school's booklet for timings by tier.

teach.heading: Repair and time-buying phrases
teach.note: Use them naturally, once or twice, not as a script.

teach.heading: Model: the ABCD answer

model.problem: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي وَسَائِلِ التَّوَاصُلِ الاِجْتِمَاعِيِّ؟
steps: Answer: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ،
Because: لِأَنَّهَا تُسَاعِدُنِي عَلَى التَّوَاصُلِ مَعَ أَقَارِبِي فِي مِصْرَ.
Contrast: لٰكِنْ يَجِبُ أَنْ نَحْذَرَ مِنْ تَضْيِيعِ الوَقْتِ.
Different time: أَمْسِ اسْتَخْدَمْتُهَا سَاعَةً وَاحِدَةً فَقَطْ.
model.answer: Answer, Because, Contrast, Different time frame

teach.note: ABCD gives every answer range.

teach.heading: Unexpected questions
bullets: Listen for the question word and the tense
Reuse a prepared sentence and adapt it
Answer in the same tense as the question
teach.note: مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ ...؟ needs the past; مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ ...؟ needs the future.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ فِي العُطْلَةِ؟ needs an answer in:
check.why: سَتَفْعَلُ is future, so answer with سَـ / سَوْفَ.

practice.q: Give an ABCD answer: هَلْ تُحِبُّ القِرَاءَةَ؟
practice.a: For example: نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّ القِرَاءَةَ كَثِيرًا لِأَنَّهَا تُعَلِّمُنِي أَشْيَاءَ جَدِيدَةً، لٰكِنِّي لَا أَجِدُ وَقْتًا كَافِيًا. الأُسْبُوعَ المَاضِي قَرَأْتُ كِتَابًا عَنْ تَارِيخِ الأَنْدَلُسِ.
practice.model:
A: نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّ القِرَاءَةَ.
B: لِأَنَّهَا ...
C: لٰكِنِّي ...
D: الأُسْبُوعَ المَاضِي قَرَأْتُ ...

practice.q: Ask the examiner to repeat the question.
practice.a: هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُعِيدَ السُّؤَالَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟

independent.q: Core (Group B): mock conversation in breakout pairs, Theme 1, five questions each, using ABCD; partner ticks a checklist. Group A: write ABCD answers to the same five questions in the portal response box.
independent.a: Checklist: opinion, reason, connective, second time frame, accuracy of verbs.
independent.model: Teacher and a confident pupil model one question and answer live.

independent.q: Extend: Write two unexpected questions for Theme 1 and answer them.
independent.a: For example: مَنْ كَانَ صَدِيقَكَ المُفَضَّلَ فِي المَدْرَسَةِ الاِبْتِدَائِيَّةِ؟

independent.q: Stretch: Re-record one answer adding a subjunctive (أَنْ + verb) and a conditional.
independent.a: For example: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ أَكْثَرَ، وَلَوْ كَانَ عِنْدِي وَقْتٌ لَقَرَأْتُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

exit.q: What does D stand for in ABCD? A) a different time frame B) a definition C) a description
Big question: what will you do if you get a question you did not expect?
exit.a: Use a time-buying phrase, listen for the tense, adapt a prepared sentence.

lessons.homework: Group B: record (audio only) three Theme 1 answers with ABCD for Draft 1 in the booklet. Group A: write the same as practice for Paper 2.
lessons.send: SEND: ABCD prompt card. EAL: phrase bank with English. Stretch: aim for 45 seconds per answer without notes.
