lessons.unit: Exam skills: Papers 1 to 4 (all five themes)
lessons.title: Listening Paper: strategies, numbers and traps
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I catch the exact detail in an extract I hear only twice?
objectives: Use the reading time to predict
Listen for numbers, negatives and distractors
Answer a multi-detail listening question accurately
successCriteria: All: identify the main topic and one detail
Most: record numbers, times and negatives accurately
Some: avoid distractors by listening to the whole sentence
lessons.crossCurricular: English: listening for detail; Maths: numbers and times
lessons.smsc: Moral and social: attentive listening (iṣghāʾ) shows respect
starter: Retrieval: say '8:30' and '3:15' in Arabic.
Say the Arabic for 'left' and 'right'.
Say 'twenty pounds' and 'five nights'.

teach.heading: Before, during, after
bullets: Use reading time: underline question words
Predict the answer type: number, place, reason
First hearing: gist; second: confirm detail
Never leave a blank: write an answer
teach.note: Per the spec file each extract is heard twice and the first five minutes include reading time. Questions in English at Foundation Section A, with different formats at Higher: check the SAMs. Teach pupils to write short answers (a word or a number) and to listen to the end of the sentence before deciding: speakers often correct themselves (ليس ... بل ...). Practise note-taking with abbreviations in English.

teach.heading: Sounds that trap
teach.note: Say each pair twice. Pupils write which they hear on mini-whiteboards. Then they listen to a full sentence. Teach the habit of checking the number against context (a price, a time, a date). The singular and plural number words may sound similar but the noun and the context disambiguate.

teach.heading: Practice script (teacher reads twice)

quote.text: تَبْدَأُ الرِّحْلَةُ فِي الثَّامِنَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ صَبَاحًا وَلَيْسَ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ. سَيَكُونُ الْجَوُّ بَارِدًا وَلَكِنَّهُ مُشْمِسٌ. اِحْضُرُوا مَعَكُمْ غَدَاءً وَقُبَّعَةً وَخَمْسَةَ جُنَيْهَاتٍ لِلْمَتْحَفِ.
quote.source: Original practice listening script (teacher reads aloud twice)

teach.note: Teacher: read this slowly, twice, at natural pace, with a pause between readings. Do not show it. Pupils answer the questions in the practice section. This is an original script, not an exam extract. Tell pupils that a speaker 'correcting' themselves is a standard trap: the time is 8:30 and NOT 9.

teach.heading: Model: answering a trap question

model.problem: After two hearings: 'What time does the trip start?' (script above)
steps: Listen for the time phrase: فِي الثَّامِنَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ = at half past eight
Notice the correction: وَلَيْسَ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ = and not at nine
Write the answer in English with the time of day: صَبَاحًا = in the morning

teach.note: Show how to record the detail after hearing it. Then the notes to the answer. Emphasise that the speaker says it is not at nine. Pupils then answer the other questions themselves from the second reading.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What will the weather be like?
check.why: بَارِدًا وَلَكِنَّهُ مُشْمِسٌ = cold but sunny. The others mix the weather words or add details that are not in the script.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A and C are distractors from the script; D is a different item. Ask pupils to show the phrase they heard that rules out nine o'clock.

practice: Listening practice: teacher reads the script twice; answer: (a) time; (b) weather; (c) three things to bring; (d) the amount of money.
Listen to a short extract of a pupil reading numbers and write them as digits.
Compare answers in pairs and say which phrase gave you each answer.
independent: Core: answer the script questions fully in English.
Extend: write your own 40-word listening script with a trap.
Stretch: swap scripts with a partner and answer theirs, then explain the trap.
exit: Write the English for 'وَلَيْسَ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ'.
Give two strategies for the listening paper.
lessons.homework: Listen to a short Arabic news item or recording and write five details in English.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: allow pauses and give a glossary of the script. Stretch: listen to unfamiliar topics at natural speed.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Bringing the world together (5.1); revision begins; mock
lessons.title: Grammar with Arabic terms: i'rab of nominal and verbal sentences
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I explain why an Arabic word ends the way it does?
objectives: To understand how to analyse (i'rab) the main parts of nominal and verbal sentences, including كَانَ and إِنَّ, using Arabic terms
successCriteria: All: label مُبْتَدَأ، خَبَر، فِعْل، فَاعِل، مَفْعُول بِهِ
Most: explain the case changes after كَانَ and إِنَّ
Some: write a full i'rab line for a word in exam style
lessons.crossCurricular: English: grammatical function (subject, object, complement)
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the Arabic grammar tradition that protected correct reading of the Qur'an

keywords.def: subject / predicate of a nominal sentence

hook.text: In إِنَّ اللّٰهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ, why does اللّٰهَ end with fathah when it usually starts a sentence with dammah?
hook.a: إِنَّ makes its noun accusative (اسم إنّ منصوب) and its predicate stays nominative.

islamicLink.text: Arabic grammar was written down early in Islamic history so that the Qur'an would be read correctly. The phrase إِنَّ اللّٰهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ appears many times in the Qur'an, for example al-Baqarah 2:173.

starter.q: Bismillah. The doer of a verb is the: A) فَاعِل B) مَفْعُول بِهِ

teach.heading: Nominal sentence
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. الطَّالِبُ مُجْتَهِدٌ: both nominative.

teach.heading: Verbal sentence
teach.note: كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ: the student wrote the lesson.

teach.heading: كَانَ and إِنَّ
teach.note: Sisters of كَانَ: أَصْبَحَ، لَيْسَ، مَا زَالَ. Sisters of إِنَّ: أَنَّ، لٰكِنَّ، لَعَلَّ.

teach.heading: Model: an i'rab line

model.problem: Analyse بَارِدًا in كَانَ الجَوُّ بَارِدًا.
steps: Role: خَبَرُ كَانَ
Case: مَنْصُوبٌ
Sign: وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ (here with tanwin)
Full line: خَبَرُ كَانَ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ الظَّاهِرَةُ
model.answer: خَبَرُ كَانَ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ الظَّاهِرَةُ

teach.note: Role, case, sign: the exam pattern.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: In لَيْسَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا, طَوِيلًا is:
check.why: لَيْسَ is a sister of كَانَ: its predicate is accusative.

practice.q: Analyse الكِتَابَ in قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الكِتَابَ.
practice.a: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ الظَّاهِرَةُ
practice.model:
Find the verb: قَرَأَ; the doer: أَحْمَدُ.
The thing read: الكِتَابَ = object.
Role, case, sign.

practice.q: Add إِنَّ and fix the endings: المُعَلِّمُ لَطِيفٌ.
practice.a: إِنَّ المُعَلِّمَ لَطِيفٌ.

independent.q: Core (portal quiz, 4AA1 style): give the i'rab of the underlined words in six sentences (worksheet), e.g. أَصْبَحَ الطَّقْسُ مُمْطِرًا; لَعَلَّ الاِمْتِحَانَ سَهْلٌ.
independent.a: مُمْطِرًا: خَبَرُ أَصْبَحَ مَنْصُوبٌ...؛ الاِمْتِحَانَ: اسْمُ لَعَلَّ مَنْصُوبٌ...؛ سَهْلٌ: خَبَرُ لَعَلَّ مَرْفُوعٌ... (full key on the worksheet)
independent.model: Teacher does the first sentence fully, saying role, case and sign.

independent.q: Extend (Group B, 1AA0): correct the endings in five sentences from your own writing (spot the case after كَانَ, إِنَّ, prepositions).
independent.a: Corrected sentences with reasons

independent.q: Stretch: analyse a dual and a sound masculine plural: إِنَّ الطَّالِبَيْنِ مُجْتَهِدَانِ.
independent.a: الطَّالِبَيْنِ: اسْمُ إِنَّ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ اليَاءُ لِأَنَّهُ مُثَنًّى؛ مُجْتَهِدَانِ: خَبَرُ إِنَّ مَرْفُوعٌ وَعَلَامَةُ رَفْعِهِ الأَلِفُ لِأَنَّهُ مُثَنًّى

exit.q: After إِنَّ, its noun is: A) مَنْصُوب B) مَرْفُوع C) مَجْرُور
Big question: what three things does an i'rab line give?
exit.a: The word's role, its case and the sign of the case.

lessons.homework: Group A: i'rab of ten words from a past paper grammar section. Group B: ten-sentence ending correction sheet.
lessons.send: SEND: role-case-sign frame. EAL: term glossary with English. Stretch: the five nouns (أَبُوكَ، أَخَاكَ) and their signs.

lessons.title: School subjects: favourites, hardest and most useful
lessons.bigQuestion: Which subjects matter most to me, and why?
objectives: Name school subjects in Arabic
Give opinions with reasons about subjects
Use comparatives and superlatives for subjects
successCriteria: All: say your favourite subject and why
Most: say which subject is hardest or easiest
Some: compare two subjects and explain which is more useful
lessons.crossCurricular: Careers education: choosing subjects
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: seeking beneficial knowledge
starter: Retrieval: say 'I go to school by bus'.
Retrieval: say the school day starts at eight.
Retrieval: say 'I like football because it is fun'.

teach.heading: Subjects
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Revise any subjects pupils know and teach the rest. Note that الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ and الْعُلُومُ are plural in form: agreement is treated in the sentences below. Use only what pupils study. The subject list is for recognition and use in speaking. Check before use: Qur'an, Surat Ta-Ha 20:114 (Arabic specialist to check the text)

teach.heading: Opinions and reasons
bullets: مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْعُلُومُ - my favourite subject is science
لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ وَمُفِيدَةٌ - because it is enjoyable and useful
لَا أُحِبُّ التَّارِيخَ لِأَنَّهُ مُمِلٌّ - I do not like history because it is boring
أَسْتَمْتِعُ بِدَرْسِ الْفَنِّ - I enjoy the art lesson
teach.note: Teach لِأَنَّهَا for a feminine subject, لِأَنَّهُ for a masculine one (التَّارِيخُ). Ask pupils to check the pronoun matches the noun. Teach أَسْتَمْتِعُ بِ (I enjoy). Encourage varied opinions, not only 'like' and 'dislike'.

teach.heading: Hardest, easiest, most useful

left.title: Superlative
points: أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ - the hardest subject for me is maths
أَسْهَلُ مَادَّةٍ هِيَ الْفَنُّ - the easiest subject is art

right.title: Comparative
points: الْعُلُومُ أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً مِنَ الْفَنِّ - science is more useful than art
التَّارِيخُ أَصْعَبُ مِنَ الْجُغْرَافْيَا - history is harder than geography

teach.note: Superlative = أَفْعَلُ + indefinite singular noun (أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ). Comparative = أَفْعَلُ + مِنْ. أَصْعَبُ and أَسْهَلُ are diptotes (no tanwin). Note أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً for 'more useful' as a pattern for adjectives that do not take أَفْعَلُ. Higher-tier work should use both.

teach.heading: Model: my subjects

model.problem: Write: 'My favourite subject is science because it is enjoyable. The hardest subject for me is maths. Science is more useful than art.'
steps: 'My favourite subject is science' = مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْعُلُومُ
'because it is enjoyable' = لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ
'The hardest subject for me is maths' = أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ
'Science is more useful than art' = الْعُلُومُ أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً مِنَ الْفَنِّ
model.answer: مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ هِيَ الْعُلُومُ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ. أَصْعَبُ مَادَّةٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ لِي هِيَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ. الْعُلُومُ أَكْثَرُ فَائِدَةً مِنَ الْفَنِّ.

teach.note: Highlight that العلوم takes a feminine singular pronoun (لِأَنَّهَا) in this sentence. Arabic specialist to check the agreement choices and diptote endings. In Arabic exams, vowelling is not expected, so also show the unvowelled version.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence means 'Maths is harder than history'?
check.why: أَصْعَبُ مِنَ places maths first. B means 'the hardest subject', C reverses the comparison, D is ungrammatical.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask which word means 'than' (مِنْ). If pupils choose C, check who is being compared with whom.

teach.heading: Knowledge as a value
bullets: رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا - my Lord, increase me in knowledge
الْعِلْمُ يَنْفَعُنِي - knowledge benefits me
teach.note: Use the ayah as a moment of reflection, not a translation task. Link to why studying even the hardest subject is worthwhile. Verify the reference with an Arabic or Islamic studies colleague before use.

practice: Say your favourite subject and give a reason.
Say which subject is hardest for you.
Translate: 'Geography is easier than history.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about your subjects, with opinions and reasons.
Extend: add a comparative and a superlative.
Stretch: write 100 words: 'Which subjects will help my future?'
exit: Write your favourite subject and one reason.
Write one comparison between two subjects.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about your timetable and your opinions of each subject.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: subject picture cards and sentence frames. Stretch: use the pattern أَكْثَرُ ... مِنْ and a relative clause.

lessons.unit: Unit 4.1: Using languages beyond the classroom
lessons.title: Arabic for travel and for work
lessons.bigQuestion: How could Arabic help me when I travel and in a future job?
objectives: Explain how languages help when travelling
Explain how languages help in employment
Use conditional sentences and the future
successCriteria: All: say one way Arabic helps when travelling
Most: say one way it helps in a job
Some: use إِذَا ... فَ to link languages and future plans
lessons.crossCurricular: Careers education; Languages: language learning
lessons.smsc: Cultural: respecting people through their language
starter: Retrieval: say 'I speak English and a little Arabic'.
Retrieval: say 'tomorrow I will travel'.
Retrieval: say 'I want to visit Cairo'.

teach.heading: Arabic when travelling
bullets: أَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَ السُّكَّانِ - I talk with the locals
أَسْأَلُ عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ - I ask about the way
أَفْهَمُ الْقَائِمَةَ - I understand the menu
أَتَعَرَّفُ عَلَى ثَقَافَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ - I get to know a new culture
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Ask pupils if they have used Arabic while travelling. Note مَعَ and عَنْ after the verbs. Qur'an 49:13 speaks of peoples and tribes made so that they may know one another (verify the reference and wording before quoting). Keep pupil experience central.

teach.heading: Arabic at work
teach.note: These are masculine forms; add taa marbuta for a woman (مُتَرْجِمَةٌ, مُرْشِدَةٌ). Idāfa structure for the last two: first noun has no al-, last noun carries al-. Ask which of these jobs could use two languages.

teach.heading: Why languages matter
bullets: الشَّرِكَاتُ تَبْحَثُ عَنْ مُوَظَّفِينَ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ لُغَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً - companies look for staff who speak many languages
إِتْقَانُ لُغَةٍ ثَانِيَةٍ مَيْزَةٌ - mastering a second language is an advantage
اللُّغَاتُ تَفْتَحُ فُرَصًا جَدِيدَةً - languages open new opportunities
teach.note: Relative clause after an indefinite noun has no relative pronoun: مُوَظَّفِينَ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ. Point out the plural of the participle (مُوَظَّفُونَ becomes مُوَظَّفِينَ after عَنْ). Link to the pupils' own plans. Teach 'because' and 'advantage' words for writing.

teach.heading: Model: future plans

model.problem: Write: 'If I speak Arabic well, I will be able to work in a hotel in Cairo. I want to be a tour guide.'
steps: 'If I speak Arabic well' = إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا
'I will be able to work' = فَسَأَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ
'in a hotel in Cairo' = فِي فُنْدُقٍ فِي الْقَاهِرَةِ
'I want to be a tour guide' = أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُرْشِدًا سِيَاحِيًّا
model.answer: إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا فَسَأَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ فِي فُنْدُقٍ فِي الْقَاهِرَةِ. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُرْشِدًا سِيَاحِيًّا.

teach.note: A past-form verb after إِذَا has a future meaning. After أَنْ the verb ends in -a (أَعْمَلَ, أَكُونَ). After كَانَ/يَكُونُ the predicate is accusative (مُرْشِدًا سِيَاحِيًّا). Arabic specialist to check.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What does إِذَا تَكَلَّمْتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ فَسَأَعْمَلُ مُتَرْجِمًا mean?
options: If I speak Arabic, I will work as a translator
I spoke Arabic and worked as a translator
I never speak Arabic as a translator
When I worked, I spoke Arabic
check.why: إِذَا + past verb signals a future condition, and سَأَعْمَلُ is future. B and D are real past, C is wrong.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Many pupils will translate the first verb as past; remind them of the conditional form.

practice: Say one way Arabic helps when you travel.
Name one job that uses languages.
Translate: 'I want to work as a translator in the future.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about using languages when travelling and at work.
Extend: add a conditional sentence with إِذَا.
Stretch: write 100 words: 'Arabic and my future'.
exit: Write one job where a second language helps.
Write: 'I will travel to Cairo.'
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about how languages could help you in a future job.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: job picture cards and sentence frames. Stretch: add two reasons with لِأَنَّ and a conditional.

lessons.title: Volunteering and training: giving time and gaining skills
lessons.bigQuestion: How do volunteering and training help me and other people?
objectives: Talk about volunteering and who it helps
Talk about training and skills
Use past tense and future tense to describe experience and plans

teach.heading: Volunteering

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: I will volunteer in the summer

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Use real examples (masjid, food bank, charity shop). The believers are like a building, each part strengthening the other (Bukhari and Muslim): a paraphrase to use in discussion. Note الْمُحْتَاجِينَ is a plural participle in the accusative.

teach.heading: Training and skills
bullets: أَخَذْتُ دَوْرَةً فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ - I took a first-aid course
أَكْتَسِبُ خِبْرَةً وَمَهَارَاتٍ - I gain experience and skills
التَّدْرِيبُ يُسَاعِدُنِي عَلَى إِيجَادِ وَظِيفَةٍ - training helps me find a job
teach.note: Teach أَخَذْتُ دَوْرَةً (I took a course). Note فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ (first aid). The masdar إِيجَادِ follows عَلَى. Ask pupils what training they might choose: first aid, coding, languages, sport coaching. Use real options.

teach.heading: Model: what I did and what I learnt

model.problem: Write: 'Last summer I volunteered at a charity. I learnt new skills. Next year I will take a first-aid course.'
steps: 'Last summer I volunteered' = الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ تَطَوَّعْتُ
'at a charity' = فِي جَمْعِيَّةٍ خَيْرِيَّةٍ
'I learnt new skills' = تَعَلَّمْتُ مَهَارَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً
'Next year I will take a first-aid course' = فِي السَّنَةِ الْقَادِمَةِ سَآخُذُ دَوْرَةً فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ
model.answer: الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ تَطَوَّعْتُ فِي جَمْعِيَّةٍ خَيْرِيَّةٍ. تَعَلَّمْتُ مَهَارَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً. فِي السَّنَةِ الْقَادِمَةِ سَآخُذُ دَوْرَةً فِي الْإِسْعَافَاتِ الْأَوَّلِيَّةِ.

teach.note: Three-tense writing: past, past, future. Note the adverbial accusative الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ (last summer). Pupils who add a reason with لِأَنَّ move up the mark scheme. Arabic specialist to check the future form سَآخُذُ.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence means 'I will volunteer in the summer'?
check.why: سَـ gives the future. B is past, C is a habit and D is 'I will not'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask pupils to underline the future marker.

practice: Say where you volunteer or could volunteer.
Say one skill you gained.
Translate: 'I will take a training course next year.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about volunteering and training.
Extend: add what you learnt and a future plan.
Stretch: write 100 words: 'How volunteering and training prepare me for work'.
exit: Write one place you could volunteer.
Write one thing training gives you.

Retrieval: say 'my father works in a shop'.
Retrieval: say 'I want to go to university'.

teach.heading: Jobs and professions
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Pupils choose professions that interest them. Show how the feminine is formed with taa marbuta. Arabic names for jobs often follow the pattern مُفَعِّل or فَاعِل: ask pupils to spot it. Revise from earlier jobs lesson but go beyond it.

teach.heading: Describing a job
bullets: أَبِي يَعْمَلُ مُحَاسِبًا - my father works as an accountant
الْوَظِيفَةُ بِدَوَامٍ جُزْئِيٍّ - the job is part-time
سَاعَاتُ الْعَمَلِ طَوِيلَةٌ - the working hours are long
الرَّاتِبُ جَيِّدٌ - the salary is good
teach.note: After يَعْمَلُ the job is accusative (مُحَاسِبًا): this is an accusative of state. Ask pupils to say what their parents or relatives do, only if they are comfortable. Discuss the pros and cons: hours, pay, helping people. The Prophet said that no food is better than what a man eats from the work of his own hand (Bukhari).

teach.heading: My career

left.title: My ambition
points: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُهَنْدِسًا - I want to be an engineer
أُفَضِّلُ وَظِيفَةً تُسَاعِدُ النَّاسَ - I prefer a job that helps people

right.title: Reasons
points: لِأَنَّ الرَّاتِبَ جَيِّدٌ - because the salary is good
وَلِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ - and because I like maths

teach.note: After لِأَنَّ the next noun is accusative (الرَّاتِبَ). With a pronoun, لِأَنَّنِي. The relative clause after an indefinite noun has no الَّذِي: وَظِيفَةً تُسَاعِدُ. Pupils write two ambitions with reasons.

teach.heading: Model: my career

model.problem: Write: 'I want to be a doctor because I like helping people. The job is hard but the salary is good. I will study medicine at university.'
steps: 'I want to be a doctor' = أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا
'because I like helping people' = لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ مُسَاعَدَةَ النَّاسِ
'The job is hard but the salary is good' = الْوَظِيفَةُ صَعْبَةٌ وَلَكِنَّ الرَّاتِبَ جَيِّدٌ
'I will study medicine at university' = سَأَدْرُسُ الطِّبَّ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ
model.answer: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ مُسَاعَدَةَ النَّاسِ. الْوَظِيفَةُ صَعْبَةٌ وَلَكِنَّ الرَّاتِبَ جَيِّدٌ. سَأَدْرُسُ الطِّبَّ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ.

teach.note: Notice وَلَكِنَّ with a noun in the accusative (الرَّاتِبَ). A pupil may use وَلَكِنْ with a nominative noun: both are accepted in standard Arabic. Female pupils say طَبِيبَةً. Arabic specialist to check.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What does أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مُهَنْدِسَةً mean?
options: I (female) want to be an engineer
I (male) want to be an engineer
I will not be an engineer
check.why: مُهَنْدِسَةً has taa marbuta, so the speaker is female. B has the masculine form, C is past and D is negative.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask pupils to circle the feminine marker.

practice: Say what job your relative does.
Say what job you want and one reason.
Translate: 'The job is part-time and the salary is good.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about a job you would like to do.
Extend: add pros and cons.
Stretch: write 100 words comparing two careers and choosing one.
exit: Write the Arabic for 'I want to be a nurse'.
Write one advantage of a job.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic about your future career.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: job cards with pictures and sentence frames. Stretch: add a conditional and relative clause.

hook.text: Who is your role model, and what one quality of theirs would you most like to have?
hook.a: Any answer with a reason; the Qur'an calls the Prophet ﷺ the best example (al-Ahzab 33:21).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example' (al-Ahzab 33:21). Theme 1 asks about role models; ours begins with him ﷺ.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I used to play': A) كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ B) سَأَلْعَبُ

starter.a: Who am I (family, friends, role models); daily life; cultural life (festivals, reading, sport)

teach.heading: Theme 1 at a glance
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. About 90% of teaching in Arabic in Year 11.

teach.heading: Past habits with كَانَ
bullets: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ فِي الحَدِيقَةِ
كُنَّا نَزُورُ جَدَّتِي كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ
كَانَ أَبِي يَقْرَأُ لَنَا قَبْلَ النَّوْمِ
teach.note: كَانَ (past) + present verb = used to. Agreement: كُنْتُ، كُنَّا، كَانَ، كَانَتْ.

teach.heading: Model: a top-band answer

model.problem: مَنْ قُدْوَتُكَ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
steps: قُدْوَتِي جَدِّي لِأَنَّهُ صَبُورٌ وَكَرِيمٌ جِدًّا.
عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كَانَ يَأْخُذُنِي إِلَى المَسْجِدِ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ.
هُوَ أَكْثَرُ صَبْرًا مِنْ أَيِّ شَخْصٍ أَعْرِفُهُ.
فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ سَأُحَاوِلُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَهُ.
model.answer: Opinion + reason, past habit, comparison, future

teach.note: Label the four moves; this works for 1AA0 Papers 2 and 4 and 4AA1 Paper 2.

teach.heading: Technology: for and against
teach.note: A common Paper 4 and Paper 1 reading topic.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: 'We used to visit my grandmother':
check.why: كُنَّا + present = past habit.

practice.q: Answer with a past habit: مَاذَا كُنْتَ تَفْعَلُ فِي رَمَضَانَ عِنْدَمَا كُنْتَ صَغِيرًا؟
practice.a: For example: كُنْتُ أَصُومُ نِصْفَ يَوْمٍ وَكُنْتُ أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي فِي الإِفْطَارِ.
practice.model:
Start: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا.
Past habit: كُنْتُ + أَصُومُ.
Add a second habit with وَكُنْتُ.

practice.q: Translate: My friend is more patient than me.
practice.a: صَدِيقِي أَكْثَرُ صَبْرًا مِنِّي.

independent.q: Core: Read the short text (worksheet) about a pupil's family and technology and answer six questions in Arabic (Group A) or English (Group B).
independent.a: Answers on the worksheet key; marked one mark per correct detail.
independent.model: Teacher answers question 1, underlining the key words in the text and the question.

independent.q: Extend: Write 90 words: مَنْ قُدْوَتُكَ؟ with the four moves from the model.
independent.a: Marked for range (past habit, comparison, future) and accuracy.

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of صَغِيرًا in عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا.
independent.a: خَبَرُ كَانَ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ

exit.q: What is قُدْوَة? A) role model B) relationship C) friend
Big question: name two structures that lift a Theme 1 answer.
exit.a: كَانَ + present for past habits; a comparison; three time frames; justified opinions.

hook.text: You meet the word مُسَافِرُونَ and do not know it. What clues inside the word could help you?
hook.a: Root س ف ر (travel), مُـ pattern for a person, ـُونَ plural: travellers.

islamicLink.text: Allah describes the Hajj journey: people come on foot and on every lean camel from every distant pass (al-Hajj 22:27). Travel has always been part of Muslim life.

starter.q: 'There is no airport in my town'?

teach.heading: Theme 2 at a glance
teach.note: Begin with bismillah.

teach.heading: The text

quote.text: سَافَرْتُ مَعَ أُسْرَتِي إِلَى الأُرْدُنِّ فِي الصَّيْفِ المَاضِي. نَزَلْنَا فِي فُنْدُقٍ صَغِيرٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنْ وَسَطِ عَمَّانَ. فِي اليَوْمِ الثَّانِي زُرْنَا البَتْرَاءَ، وَكَانَ الجَوُّ حَارًّا جِدًّا، لِذٰلِكَ اشْتَرَيْنَا مَاءً كَثِيرًا. أَعْجَبَنِي الطَّعَامُ، لٰكِنَّ المُشْكِلَةَ كَانَتِ الاِزْدِحَامَ فِي الشَّوَارِعِ. فِي السَّنَةِ القَادِمَةِ سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى العُمْرَةِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.
quote.source: Our own exam-style text for this lesson

teach.note: Read once for gist, once for detail. Meaning: I travelled with my family to Jordan last summer. We stayed in a small hotel near the centre of Amman. On the second day we visited Petra; it was very hot, so we bought lots of water. I liked the food, but the problem was the crowded streets. Next year we will go for Umrah, in sha' Allah.

teach.heading: Strategies
bullets: Underline the question word, then scan for it
Watch the tense: past, present or future?
Unknown word? Find the root and the pattern
teach.note: Example: اشْتَرَيْنَا: root ش ر ي (buy), ـنَا = we: we bought.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Why did they buy lots of water?
check.why: كَانَ الجَوُّ حَارًّا جِدًّا، لِذٰلِكَ اشْتَرَيْنَا مَاءً كَثِيرًا.

practice.q: أَيْنَ نَزَلَتِ الأُسْرَةُ؟
practice.a: فِي فُنْدُقٍ صَغِيرٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنْ وَسَطِ عَمَّانَ (in a small hotel near central Amman)
practice.model:
أَيْنَ asks where.
Find نَزَلْنَا (we stayed).
The answer follows: فِي فُنْدُقٍ صَغِيرٍ ...

practice.q: What was the problem?
practice.a: Crowded streets (الاِزْدِحَامُ فِي الشَّوَارِعِ)

practice.q: What are their plans for next year?
practice.a: To go for Umrah (سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى العُمْرَةِ)

independent.a: Answers on the worksheet key.

independent.q: Stretch: Translate the last two sentences of the text into English.
independent.a: I liked the food, but the problem was the crowded streets. Next year we will go for Umrah, in sha' Allah.

Big question: how do you answer without understanding every word?

lessons.title: 4AA1 summary writing: the main ideas in my own words
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I summarise an Arabic text accurately and in my own words?
objectives: To understand how to select the main ideas of a text and write them as a concise summary in my own words
successCriteria: All: identify the main idea of each paragraph
Most: rephrase ideas in my own words without copying
Some: write a summary within the word limit, linked and accurate
lessons.crossCurricular: English: summarising non-fiction (4EB1 skills)
lessons.smsc: Moral: representing other people's words fairly and accurately

hook.text: Someone asks what a long lecture was about, and you have one minute. What do you keep, and what do you leave out?
hook.a: Keep the main points; drop examples, repetition and minor details.

islamicLink.text: Allah describes the Qur'an as a Book whose verses are perfected and then explained in detail (Hud 11:1). Summarising faithfully means keeping the meaning exactly.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Main idea': A) فِكْرَة رَئِيسِيَّة B) تَفَاصِيل

teach.heading: The task
bullets: 4AA1 Paper 1 has a summary of a third text
Read the instruction: what to summarise and the word limit
Marks for content (main points) and for your own words and accuracy
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Check the current 4AA1 specification and sample assessment materials for the exact word limit and marks.

teach.heading: The text

quote.text: تُعَدُّ القِرَاءَةُ مِنْ أَهَمِّ عَادَاتِ الإِنْسَانِ، فَهِيَ تُوَسِّعُ مَعْرِفَتَهُ وَتُنَمِّي لُغَتَهُ. وَقَدْ أَصْبَحَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الشَّبَابِ يَقْضُونَ سَاعَاتٍ أَمَامَ الشَّاشَاتِ بَدَلًا مِنَ الكُتُبِ. وَلِذٰلِكَ يَنْصَحُ المُعَلِّمُونَ بِتَخْصِيصِ وَقْتٍ يَوْمِيٍّ لِلْقِرَاءَةِ، وَبِأَنْ يَقْرَأَ الآبَاءُ مَعَ أَبْنَائِهِمْ.
quote.source: Our own exam-style text for this lesson

teach.note: Meaning: Reading is one of the most important human habits; it widens knowledge and develops language. Many young people now spend hours in front of screens instead of books. So teachers advise setting a daily time for reading, and that parents read with their children.

teach.heading: Model: from text to summary

model.problem: Summarise the text in about 25 words.
steps: Idea 1: reading widens knowledge and language
Idea 2: young people prefer screens
Idea 3: advice: daily reading; parents read with children
Own words: لِلْقِرَاءَةِ فَوَائِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ لِلْعَقْلِ وَاللُّغَةِ، لٰكِنَّ الشَّبَابَ يُفَضِّلُونَ الشَّاشَاتِ، فَيَقْتَرِحُ المُعَلِّمُونَ قِرَاءَةً يَوْمِيَّةً بِمُشَارَكَةِ الأُسْرَةِ.
model.answer: Three ideas, linked, rephrased

teach.note: Compare word by word: nothing copied in long chunks.

teach.heading: Rephrasing tools
teach.note: Synonyms, a different structure, or a noun instead of a verb.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which belongs in a summary?
options: A long quotation from the text
The main ideas in your own words
